restaurants.name: 'ino
restaurants.summary: ‘ino is a modern Italian restaurant with unique dishes influenced by chef Jamie Kenyon's English background, alongside a boutique selection of Italian organic and biodynamic wines plus craft cocktails.
restaurants.description: Founded by Bottino Partnership, 'ino is a modern Italian restaurant with unique dishes influenced by chef Jamie Kenyon's English background, and offering a boutique selection of Italian organic and biodynamic wines and features craft cocktails inspired by classic Italian and English mixology. The space, designed by award-winning architect Thomas Leeser (who also designed the original Bottino), is eclectic and modern, and features works of some significant artists (most recently Joel Shapiro and John Baldessari) connecting 'ino with Bottino's legacy in the NYC art world.

restaurants.name: 1803 NYC
restaurants.summary: 1803 NYC transports guests from the Big Apple to the Big Easy with its stunning balcony seating, covered outdoor seating, and prohibition speakeasy bar, with Cajun-Creole dishes and NOLA classics and live jazz.
restaurants.description: 1803 NYC is a Tribeca restaurant inspired by New Orleans’ food, culture, and celebratory energy. Named for the Louisiana Purchase, the menu draws from Cajun-Creole traditions with dishes such as gumbo, jambalaya, seafood-forward plates, and classic New Orleans flavors, paired with a cocktail program influenced by the city’s bar culture. The space is designed for lively dining, with a warm atmosphere and programming that can include live music and seasonal celebrations. An on-site speakeasy, Bon Courage, adds an additional layer to the experience for guests.

restaurants.summary: 53 introduces an elevated blend of Asian cuisine with a contemporary edge in a chic lifestyle setting, featuring an exciting rotating installation art program in collaboration with Friedrich Petzel Gallery.
restaurants.description: 53 introduces an elevated blend of Asian cuisine with a contemporary edge in a chic lifestyle setting. Featuring an exquisite marriage of Asian flavors and unique dishes, 53 was conceived by Ahmass Fakahany and the team behind the award-winning Marea and Ai Fiori. The menu is spearheaded by acclaimed Singapore-born chef Akmal Anuar, who began his culinary journey in his parents’ hawker stand in Singapore, led one of Pellegrino World’s 50 Best Restaurants (Asia’s No. 1), and created some of the top contemporary Asian restaurants in Dubai. Designed by ICRAVE, the three-story space features a beautiful modern dining room, bustling by day and glowing by night, as well as an intimate private dining experience—all underneath MoMA’s extended wing. In the spirit of this iconic location, the globally renowned Friedrich Petzel Gallery collaborates in a curatorial partnership to showcase an exciting rotating art installation throughout the restaurant.

restaurants.summary: 8282 is a light-hearted, fresh take on Korean food on the Lower East Side.
restaurants.description: 8282 is a light-hearted, fresh take on Korean food on the Lower East Side. The name 8282 refers to Korea’s country code, +82, and has an additional meaning: The numbers, when read together, translate to a phrase that means “quickly” or “faster.” The phrase signifies a get-it-done attitude. Behind 8282 is a couple who previously ran the restaurant Pado in the East Village. Bong Le Jo had cooked in the kitchens of Perry St, Dovetail and Kissaki, and Jee Kim launched several fashion and lifestyle brands, and worked as a truffle distributor in Seoul.

restaurants.description: A Pasta Bar is an elegant Italian culinary theater in the SoHo neighborhood of Manhattan. restaurants.name: ABC Cocina
restaurants.summary: ABC Kitchen has a design of ethereal lightness, while its sister restaurant, ABC Cocina, is all dark magic.
restaurants.description: ABC Kitchen has a design of ethereal lightness, while its sister restaurant, ABC Cocina, is all dark magic. They also share an ethos of green technology via building materials and lighting, and they source their menu items from small, sustainable farmers. At this, the more casual of the two ABC eateries, chef de cuisine Ian Coogan combines influences from Spain, Mexico and Argentina for a user-friendly tapas style menu as seen through a New American prism. Reservations are recommended or there's walk-in seating available at the bar or communal table.

restaurants.name: ABC Kitchen
restaurants.summary: ABC Kitchen by Michelin starred Chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten has a passionate commitment to offering the freshest organic and local ingredients possible.
restaurants.description: ABC Kitchen by Michelin starred Chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten has a passionate commitment to offering the freshest organic and local ingredients possible. Located within ABC Carpet & Home and sharing space with its sister restaurant, ABC Cocina (which features seasonal global Latin cuisine by Jean-Georges), this restaurant is a destination for visitors and locals alike.

restaurants.name: ABC Kitchens DUMBO
restaurants.summary: ABC Kitchens’ seasonally driven menu is an evolution and combination of Jean-Georges' Manhattan restaurants, ABC Kitchen, abcV and ABC Cocina, under one roof on the DUMBO waterfront.
restaurants.description: Chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten has opened ABC Kitchens, his first-ever Brooklyn restaurant, located on the iconic DUMBO waterfront at Empire Stores. ABC Kitchens’ seasonally-driven menu is an evolution and combination of ABC Kitchen’s approach to greenmarket fare, abcV's innovative plant-based dishes and ABC Cocina's global flavors, under one roof. The industrial waterfront space features a commanding peninsula bar and a central glass enclosure that functions as a retail space, selling vintage glassware, tableware and florals, and transforms into a whimsical dinner scene by night. ABC Kitchens is also available for private dining, where guests can dine amongst vintage decor, antique chandeliers and abundant blooms.

restaurants.name: abcV
restaurants.summary: Jean-Georges Vongerichten performs magic with vegetables.
restaurants.description: Jean-Georges Vongerichten's abcV (“V” stands for vegetables) is a radiant outgrowth of Flatiron gems ABC Kitchen and ABC Cocina. The bathed-in-white showroom has a bar and communal standing table up front; in the rear is a dining room facing the windowed kitchen. Good knife skills are key for chefs here, and the dice is precise on yams and broccoli stems dotting beluga lentils flavored with black vinegar and sneaky heat from chili oil. Diners can substitute shaved crudité for pita to scoop up drop-dead gorgeous kabocha squash dip. The beverage menu is creative and wide-ranging.

images.alt: Courtesy, abcV

restaurants.name: Acadia
restaurants.summary: Executive chef Ari Bokovza's menu is inspired by Levantine traditions, brought to life through innovative preparation.
restaurants.description: Acadia strikes the perfect balance between upscale and casual, ensuring patrons feel comfortable while still indulging in a refined experience. It's a vibrant gathering place, open to all who seek a memorable night out paired with exceptional cuisine. Executive chef Ari Bokovza's menu is inspired by Levantine traditions, brought to life through innovative preparation. Each dish carries with it a rich history, reimagined with a contemporary twist. Indulge in creations like the delicate eggplant varpaccio, adorned with a veil of tuna bresaola, or savor the bold flavors of rotisserie harissa BBQ Sasso chicken and delicious shrimp shish barak.

restaurants.summary: The Langham, New York, Fifth Avenue’s signature restaurant celebrates cuisine from the Italian and French Riviera.
restaurants.description: The Langham, New York, Fifth Avenue’s signature restaurant, from acclaimed chef Michael White and the Altamarea Group, Ai Fiori celebrates cuisine from the Italian and French Riviera. The inspired menu blends traditional Italian fare with a brave, modern perspective. Ai Fiori features an inviting bar and lounge with an extensive cocktail and wine list crafted by the restaurant's renowned beverage professionals. Located a short walk up the Langham’s sweeping grand staircase to the second floor, Ai Fiori's ambiance is elegant yet welcoming. The restaurant's striking floral arrangements and décor will embrace you in warmth and refinement.

restaurants.name: Ammos Estiatorio - Grand Central
restaurants.summary: Features upscale authentic cuisine from various regions of Greece, emphasizing seafood and incorporating Mediterranean and North African influences.
restaurants.description: Open design, light woods and weathered stones conjure the sun-drenched atmosphere of the Greek islands at Ammos, which features upscale authentic Greek cuisine from various regions of Greece, emphasizing seafood and incorporating Mediterranean and North African influences. Many of the ingredients—sea salt, dried oregano, capers and caperberries—are imported from Greece, while many of the staples like olive oil, honey and halloumi cheese are produced on a family farm in Cyprus. The wine list, featuring 200 Greek wines, is supplemented by signature cocktails and an extensive list of beers, liquors and spirits.

restaurants.name: Amélie - Upper West Side
restaurants.summary: "La Petite Amélie" is smaller and more intimate than Amélie's other locations, but has the same look and vibe.
restaurants.description: Amélie Upper West Side is a newer location that the owners like to call "La Petite Amélie." It is smaller and more intimate than their other locations, but has the same look and vibe. Amélie has won Michelin recognition in the Bib Gourmand category, and the extensive selection of wine will take you all around the world with the most generous pour. Happy Hour is served every day, and their popular wine tasting flights are available all night. The French staff is welcoming, friendly and knowledgeable.

restaurants.name: Amélie - West Village
restaurants.summary: At this Greenwich Village location, the intention is to make good wine accessible, affordable and fun.
restaurants.description: Amélie has become one of the most successful wine bars in the City, attracting an eclectic crowd nightly. At this Greenwich Village location, the intention is to make good wine accessible, affordable and fun. With its euro-chic décor, sensual lighting and great bar music, Amélie has changed the way good wine is enjoyed and consumed. Patrons appreciate the generous pour, the terrific French cuisine, the international flair, and the great choice of good wines at fair prices.

restaurants.name: Animo!
restaurants.summary: Ánimo! is an authentic Mexican restaurant dedicated to honoring the rich culinary traditions of Mexico.
restaurants.description: Ánimo! is an authentic Mexican restaurant dedicated to honoring the rich culinary traditions of Mexico. The menu features classic dishes prepared with care, using high-quality ingredients and time-honored techniques—no shortcuts, nothing pre-made, and everything crafted from scratch. From their handmade tortillas to slow-cooked moles and house-marinated pastor, every bite is rooted in bold, soulful flavor. Just as essential as the food is the spirit of Mexican hospitality. Ánimo! welcomes every guest with warmth, generosity, and attention to detail, creating a dining experience that feels both elevated and deeply personal. At Ánimo!, you're not just having a meal—you're part of something meaningful.

restaurants.description: Antica Pesa Brooklyn, "your home away from Rome," opened in 2012 as the first outpost of the legendary restaurant owned and operated by the Panella family since 1922 in Rome, Italy. Antica Pesa is named after the antique scales of the 17th-century customs post in Trastevere where Antica Pesa Rome stands today. Antica Pesa Brooklyn pays homage to their homeland with a focus on the traditionally innovative dishes that transport diners directly to Rome.

restaurants.name: Aqua Kyoto
restaurants.summary: Aqua New York has two separate restaurants—Aqua Roma and Aqua Kyoto—each a master of its own cuisine to bring this unique lifestyle dining concept to the table.
restaurants.description: Aqua New York has two separate restaurants—Aqua Roma and Aqua Kyoto—each a master of its own cuisine to bring this unique lifestyle dining concept to the table. With two amazing cuisines, contemporary Japanese and Italian, served as one fabulous experience, Aqua New York offers dining on a grand scale. Order from one menu or both, wherever you are seated. The menu reads Italian from the front and Japanese from the back. Their dinners often start with a signature Japanese sushi platter to share, followed by an Italian entrée and a delicious dessert. Italian and Japanese cooking match perfectly because they both share the same culinary philosophy: using the freshest seasonal produce and preparing theme simply to let their natural flavors shine.

restaurants.summary: An intimate global restaurant in Harlem serves impressive cocktails.
restaurants.description: This modern Harlem restaurant stretches along the ground level of a townhouse and features outdoor seating in front and in a back patio. The name Archer & Goat is drawn from the husband-and-wife owners’ zodiac signs: Alex Guzman is a Sagittarius (the Archer) and Jenifar Chowdhury is a Capricorn (the Goat). Their multicultural backgrounds dictate tantalizing dishes that use or combine South American and Indian flavors, like arepas with chicken vindaloo and carne asada with crispy tostones. At brunch, look for hot chicken biscuit sliders sweetened with maple aioli and pickled strawberries.

restaurants.description: Aromi is a restaurant and pizzeria with a mission to bring classic, authentic Italian recipes to Carroll Gardens in Brooklyn. The name evokes the owners' grandparents' gardens, their fruit trees and the vegetables they grew. In Italy, that is where you will find those bushes of aromatic spices that bring out the special flavors from their childhood. Their homemade pasta, pizza, focaccia, and cocktails, are all enriched with these authentic “aromi.” Aromi has a beautiful wood oven, a cozy indoor dining room, a nice backyard, and a welcoming bar.

restaurants.name: Arthur & Sons - Murray Hill
restaurants.summary: The Isidori Family has owned and operated restaurants in the NYC area since 1954, and Arthur & Sons - Murray Hill pays homage to the NYC Italian-American scene of which they have been a part.
restaurants.description: Joe Isidori is an acclaimed Michelin-starred chef, restaurateur, and cookbook author, best known as the co-founder and co-creator of popular restaurant franchise Black Tap Craft Burgers & Beers. He's a third-generation chef whose family has owned and operated restaurants in New York’s tristate area since 1954, including his grandmother’s renowned Manhattan restaurant The Villanova, Artie’s Bar and Butcher Shop in Harlem and Artie’s Steak and Liquor Lounge in Brooklyn run by his grandfather, and Arturo’s Tavern in Westchester County and Peppino’s in Greenwich, Connecticut run by his father. Arthur & Sons - Murray Hill pays homage to the NYC Italian-American scene. Their culture is rooted in old-school food, vibes and attitude, harkening back to the '90s, "when everything in NY was just better than anywhere else!"

restaurants.description: Askili Orchard reimagines Georgian cuisine through a contemporary New York lens. Inspired by centuries-old culinary traditions from the crossroads of Europe and Asia, the menu offers lighter, elegant interpretations of classic Georgian dishes, crafted with seasonal ingredients and made-from-scratch sauces, preserves and breads. Alongside signature favorites, they also offer vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options, including their popular gluten-free Adjaruli Khachapuri. Curated by a diverse culinary team and complemented by an extensive wine program featuring Georgia and beyond, Askili Orchard invites guests to discover the rich flavors of Georgia in a warm, vibrant setting in Manhattan's West Village.

Borrowing its name from the ancient Korean word ‘Ato’ meaning gift, Atoboy first opened its doors in July of 2016, inspired by the concept of banchan: small side dishes served with every Korean meal. Atoboy has since been recognized by The New York Times, the Michelin Guide, and OAD (Opinionated About Dining) alongside global dining destinations. Atoboy currently offers a 4-course prix-fixe menu alongside a curated selection of beverages with a focus on wines.

restaurants.description: Baci & Abbracci offers traditional Neapolitan fare as well as Italian classics from all over the "Boot." The Cappiello brothers, Paolo and Mimmo, along with partner Rocco Cadolini, opened their doors in 2006 and have kept the business a family affair since its inception. Whether it's personally shopping for the freshest, local ingredients or hand making the pasta and mozzarella, Baci & Abbracci strives for excellence and authenticity. Even Mother Rosa lends a hand, making her Sorrentinian delicacies. Winner of Eat Out NY's "Best New Pizza Joint" 2007 and Michelin Guide recommended, Baci & Abbracci features a variety of pizza baked in a wood burning over imported directly from Naples.

restaurants.name: Bananas
restaurants.summary: Bananas is an expression of the chef-owners' take on Asian American food, incorporating classic Asian flavors with Western cuisine—a signature menu of American favorites with elements of Asian cooking.
restaurants.description: Bananas, a New American restaurant from chef-owners Chris Ng (previously of Blue Ribbon and Bond St) and Kyaw Lwin (previously of Yakiniku Futago, Hasalon and Michelin-starred Shmoné), is located in the East Village. Bananas is an expression of the team’s take on Asian American food, incorporating classic Asian flavors with Western cuisine. The phrase “Bananas” has previously been used as a slur to describe Asian Americans who are ‘yellow’ presenting but culturally white due to their upbringing in America. Bananas offers a signature menu of American favorites with elements of Asian cooking.

restaurants.name: Bar Lola
restaurants.summary: European bistro charm meets New York sensibility at Bar Lola, a two-floor café and cocktail bar on Restaurant Row that's inspired by Spanish wine bars and French cafés.
restaurants.description: European bistro charm meets New York sensibility at Bar Lola, a two-floor café and cocktail bar on Restaurant Row from PMac’s Hospitality Group. Inspired by Spanish wine bars and French cafés, the space centers around an art nouveau–style bar and extends to a year-round patio with a retractable roof. The playful yet polished beverage program flows from coffee to cocktails alongside natural wines. Executive chef Hesh Darwish delivers globally inspired, shareable dishes tailored to daytime café service and evening cocktails.

restaurants.name: Bar Mercer
restaurants.summary: Chef Preston Clark’s gastropub-inspired menu features a concise selection of exceptional dishes, including an expertly curated raw bar, skillfully prepared small plates, and hearty mains.
restaurants.description: Nestled in SoHo in downtown Manhattan, Bar Mercer blends John McDonald’s renowned hospitality with chef Preston Clark’s culinary artistry in an intimate setting accented by deep red walls, rich woods, and vintage fixtures. The gastropub-inspired menu features a concise selection of exceptional dishes, including an expertly curated raw bar, skillfully prepared small plates, and hearty mains. Signature offerings range from East and West Coast oysters and hamachi crudo to perfectly seared branzino and grass-fed filet au poivre. Nightly blackboard specials further highlight seasonal creativity. Complementing the cuisine is an extensive wine list featuring acclaimed global regions, alongside premium spirits such as rare single malts, small-batch bourbons, artisanal mezcals, and vintage-dated rums.

restaurants.name: Barano
restaurants.summary: Fire-roasted, grandma-inspired Italian food in Williamsburg.
restaurants.description: Barano is a charming Italian restaurant helmed by Albert Di Meglio, who named it for his grandmother’s birthplace on the tiny island of Ischia near Naples. She instilled in him a passion for the art of cooking, a heritage that he expresses in his hickory-smoked mozzarella, handmade pastas, pizza and wood-fired main courses. Di Meglio, formerly of Little Italy’s Rubirosa, is supported by a staff skilled in helping navigate the mostly Italian wine list and seasonal cocktail menu. You can book ahead at this Williamsburg destination, or arrive spontaneously and dine at the bar.

restaurants.name: Becco
restaurants.summary: Lidia Bastianich and her son, Joe, opened Becco in 1993, and since then it has been providing New York diners with outstanding service.
restaurants.description: The name Becco is derived from the Italian verb, beccare, which means "to peck, nibble or savor something in a discriminating way." Lidia Bastianich and her son, Joe, opened Becco in 1993, and since then it has been providing New York diners with outstanding service. Located on New York's famed Restaurant Row in the Theatre District, Becco is open seven days a week for lunch and dinner. Becco is most famous for its innovative pasta tasting menu and extensive wine list, featuring more than 100 bottles of wine, all priced at $40.

restaurants.description: Ben and Jack Sinanaj, long-time waiters at Peter Luger’s, have opened a classic steakhouse all their own. In addition to offering prime dry-aged porterhouse steaks, including their signature 44-ouncer, as well as other flavorful cuts of meat, the restaurant offers an array of seafood, from fresh oysters to a hefty four-pound lobster. If you can manage to squeeze in dessert, try the hot-fudge sundae or the German apple strudel. An extensive wine list is available too.

restaurants.name: BKK New York
restaurants.summary: With fresh takes on NYC staples, like the BKK Hot Dog with homemade Thai pork sausage, BKK serves innovative spins on NYC dishes, while delivering authentic Thai flavors, and traditional homestyle classics.
restaurants.description: BKK New York is a modern Thai street-food restaurant located in Midtown Manhattan. Inspired by Bangkok street food, BKK creatively combines the cultures and flavors of Bangkok and New York City. With fresh takes on NYC staples, like the BKK Hot Dog with homemade Thai pork sausage, to a brisket sandwich with Thai spicy beef jus, BKK serves innovative spins on NYC dishes, while delivering authentic Thai flavors, and traditional homestyle classics like Kao Moo Deng Moo Krob, Pad Thai and Kra Pow Gai Kai Dow, to name a few. BKK reimagines vibrant Bangkok street food culture with a contemporary and elevated twist, blending the energy of Bangkok’s streets with the cosmopolitan spirit of NYC, creating a dining experience that feels global yet distinctly Thai.

restaurants.description: Blackbarn is an American restaurant serving local, artisanal food in the comfort of a modern barn setting. Opened in 2015 overlooking Madison Square Park, the restaurant is the creation of chef John Doherty, former executive chef of New York's Waldorf Astoria, and designer Mark Zeff. restaurants.description: Located in Times Square just steps from Broadway, Blue Fin is a modern seafood and sushi restaurant inside the iconic W New York–Times Square Hotel. Blue Fin offers an elevated dining experience where refined design, premium ingredients, and Midtown Manhattan’s vibrant energy meet. A favorite among theater‑goers, NYC locals, and international visitors, Blue Fin NYC specializes in fresh seafood, expertly crafted sushi, and USDA Prime steaks. Its sleek, contemporary atmosphere provides a calm escape from Times Square, making it ideal for pre‑theater dining, business meals, date nights, and special occasions in Manhattan.

restaurants.summary: This rustic-chic restaurant and wine bar on Manhattan's Upper East Side has a welcoming vibe and an easy, all-day rhythm.
restaurants.description: This rustic-chic restaurant and wine bar on Manhattan's Upper East Side has a welcoming vibe and an easy, all-day rhythm. The space has a relaxed and intimate feel, thanks to the toasty details and cozy energy. The American and Italian style of the food is paired with clever bistro fare. Guests can sit down for a meal that feels both fancy and casual from morning to night. The experience is meant to feel personal, simple, and full of neighborhood charm, whether you're just stopping by to catch up, have a glass of wine, or stay for dinner. This wine bar has a unique identity because of the way it combines style, comfort, and thoughtful dining.

restaurants.description: Bocca Di Bacco is an Italian restaurant located near the Theatre District that is popular with celebrities, tourists and native New Yorkers. It has two additional locations in nearby neighborhoods Hell's Kitchen and Chelsea. Whether for drinks after work or dining before or after a show, Bocca Di Bacco aims to satisfy. Known for top-notch creative Italian cuisine including homemade pasta, meats and seafood, this restaurant also has an excellent wine selection with 500 of the best bottles from renowned Italian wineries.

restaurants.name: Bond 45
restaurants.summary: This enormous, bi-level, Italian-ish venue offers a huge variety of meals and dishes.
restaurants.description: Restaurateur Shelly Fireman engineered a two-block move for Bond 45, keeping the name although it’s on 46th Street now, across from the Richard Rodgers Theatre (where Hamilton is in residence). The enormous, bi-level, Italian-ish venue offers breakfast all day, a lavish antipasti bar and, in the downstairs bar, postshow happy hour discounts nightly after 9pm. Thin-crust pizzas, pasta, big salads, grilled fish and burgers with cacio e pepe-dusted fries are available for lunch or dinner.

restaurants.name: Bonsaii Tapas & Wine Bar
restaurants.summary: The cuisine at Bonsaii Tapas & Wine Bar is inspired by international tapas, putting an updated spin on classic dishes and bringing creative new ones.
restaurants.description: Gather your crew for an unforgettable tapas-style dining experience accompanied with a fine selection of wines and crafted cocktails. With more than 10 years of experience in hospitality, aspiring restauranteurs Kevin Cardenas and Ruben Cabrera launched themselves with their first venture, Ceviche Fussion, which was an overwhelming success. An opportunity arose that bore this intimate and inviting venue, Bonsaii Tapas & Wine Bar, inspired by the Japanese bonsai tree (a miniature tree cultivated to resemble nature in a modest space and nurtured with artistic interaction). Bonsaii Tapas & Wine Bar is the ultimate representation of its namesake. Their cuisine is inspired by international tapas, putting an updated spin on classic dishes and bringing creative new ones, so every patron will feel welcomed and find something of their taste.

restaurants.name: Boro Brine
restaurants.summary: Boro Brine is a seafood restaurant and raw bar that celebrates the rich diversity of NYC's food cultures while showcasing local and coastal seafood.
restaurants.description: Boro Brine is a seafood restaurant and raw bar that celebrates the rich diversity of NYC's food cultures while showcasing local and coastal seafood. Their menu blends flavors and techniques inspired by the City's vibrant culinary scene, offering dishes that are both familiar and exciting. From classic oysters to innovative crudos and a take on the Fish-O-Fillet, every bite highlights sustainable, responsibly sourced seafood. Paired with handcrafted cocktails and curated wines, the space invites guests to experience the best of the ocean and the City.

restaurants.name: BOTA Supper Club
restaurants.summary: An exclusive 21+ venue, BOTA Supper Club is Staten Island’s hottest destination for elevated modern American cuisine, where chic vibes meet sultry sophistication.
restaurants.description: BOTA Supper Club is Staten Island’s hottest destination for elevated modern American cuisine, where chic vibes meet sultry sophistication. An exclusive 21+ venue, BOTA is where members get priority access to unforgettable nights of fine dining, music, and entertainment. Embrace the evening in style—BOTA encourages guests to dress elegantly for the occasion. Tailored shorts are welcome, but athletic wear and baseball caps are not permitted. Dress to impress and enjoy a night of refined luxury.

restaurants.name: Bottino
restaurants.summary: Since 1997, Bottino has offered classic and contemporary Tuscan Italian cuisine and boutique wines—as well as house cocktails and a bar menu—steps from the vibrant West Chelsea gallery scene.
restaurants.description: Since 1997, Bottino has offered classic and contemporary Tuscan Italian cuisine and boutique wines—as well as house cocktails and a bar menu—steps from the vibrant West Chelsea gallery scene. From a century-old hardware store, architect Thomas Leeser fashioned a mid-century modern eatery with a beautiful garden. Lovely for a romantic dinner, an evening with family or friends, Bottino's private dining spaces make it an ideal venue for large events as well.

restaurants.name: Boucherie Union Square
restaurants.summary: Boucherie Union Square is a traditional French brasserie and steakhouse, celebrating Joie de Vivre, that prepares a menu of French classics and timeless bistro favorites, in addition to dry-aged steaks.
restaurants.description: Boucherie Union Square is a traditional French brasserie and steakhouse celebrating Joie de Vivre. The restaurant features an ample menu of French classics and timeless bistro favorites, such as the Soupe à l’Oignon and Steak Frites, in addition to delectable dry-aged meats. Alongside an extensive wine list, guests can enjoy signature cocktails, absinthe drinks, non-alcoholic options, craft beers, and more. Surrounded by walls of majestic wooden-framed mirrors and original Belle Époque posters, seating at this Union Square location varies among pristine white marble and wood bistro tables, cozy burgundy leather booths, a 32-foot handmade pewter bar, and an option for a 40-guest private room, to make the 222-seat restaurant feel timeless.

restaurants.summary: Boucherie West Village is a traditional French brasserie and steakhouse, celebrating Joie de Vivre, that prepares a menu of French classics and timeless bistro favorites, in addition to dry-aged steaks.
restaurants.description: Boucherie West Village is a traditional French brasserie and steakhouse celebrating Joie de Vivre in the West Village. The restaurant features an ample menu of French classics and timeless bistro favorites, such as the Mousse de Foie Gras and the signature Boucherie Burger, in addition to delectable dry-aged meats. Alongside an extensive wine list, guests can enjoy signature cocktails, absinthe drinks, non-alcoholic options, craft beers, and more. Located in the building that used to house the prominent Circle Repertory Theater, the 320-seat restaurant provides a diverse array of dining options from the spacious dining room, a seat at the butcher counter, the intimate second-floor gallery with private dining and outdoor cafe.

restaurants.name: Brass & the Tusk Bar
restaurants.summary: Through the Art Deco lobby of the historic Evelyn Hotel, find The Tusk Bar for bright takes on classic cocktails, raw bar and seafood-driven small plates, and Brass, an NYC take on the French brasserie.
restaurants.description: Through the Art Deco lobby of the historic Evelyn Hotel, find Brass & The Tusk Bar. Tusk is a jewel of a classic cocktail and oyster bar, named one of Esquire’s "Best Bars in America, 2024." Look for bright takes on classic cocktails, raw bar and seafood-driven small plates. The glamorous bar room marries the spirit of the roaring '20s with the convivial attitude of mid-century cocktail parties, sharing the timelessness of a warm welcome, a well-made drink, a freshly shucked oyster...and a good time. Located through the bar, Brass restaurant is a New York City brasserie that takes inspiration from the style of French brasseries but without adhering to their playbook. Brass showcases the playful contemporary spirit that characterizes chefs Jeremiah Stone and Fabian Von Hauske Valtierra’s cuisine.

restaurants.name: Bustan
restaurants.summary: Bustan blossoms with a contemporary pan-Mediterranean vibe that extends the shores of Southern Europe, Western Asian and North Africa to Manhattan's Upper West Side.
restaurants.description: Bustan—meaning "garden" or "orchard" in Hebrew, Arabic and ancient Aramaic—blossoms with a contemporary pan-Mediterranean vibe that extends the shores of Southern Europe, Western Asian and North Africa to Manhattan's Upper West Side. Showcasing the region's culinary diversity, Bustan stands out with a distinctive palate-enticing multicultural approach to food and drink. That multicultural approach extends to the look of their intimate space, which draws from a broad spectrum of Mediterranean motifs, masterfully melded to create an exuberantly energized atmosphere. That atmosphere encourages the epicurean exploration of their menus with the polished guidance of a congenial staff that's well-versed in the provenance of their food and beverage offerings. Bustan realizes the vision of proprietor Tuvia Feldman to present New Yorkers with the eclectic gastronomic style and fabled hospitality of Israel.

restaurants.summary: Daniel Boulud's tribute to the original Café Boulud in Lyon, France, serves finely executed cuisine.
restaurants.description: Daniel Boulud’s tribute to the original Café Boulud in Lyon, France, this version doesn’t evoke a sense of “town folk charm” like the original does, but it is quite comfortable and well appointed with murals of the French countryside, elegant place settings and even sidewalk seating. The avuncular clientele here enjoy the finely executed cuisine, and the standouts include the Hudson Valley foie gras, the braised octopus terrine and the English pea raviolini with bacon.

restaurants.name: Café Fleuri
restaurants.summary: Café Fleuri brings the sun-soaked flavors of Southern France to the Financial District.
restaurants.description: Café Fleuri brings the sun-soaked flavors of Southern France to the Financial District. Helmed by Michelin-starred chef Eduard Frauneder, the kitchen turns out Provençal classics and Mediterranean-inspired plates in a warm, light-filled room just off Washington Street. From a crisp Salade Niçoise to a perfectly grilled Loup de Mer, every dish is rooted in seasonal produce and unfussy French technique. Café Fleuri is open for lunch and dinner, Monday through Saturday.

restaurants.name: Calle Dão - Bryant Park
restaurants.summary: Calle Dão pays homage to Havana’s once-thriving El Barrio Chino (Chinatown), once the largest such community in Latin America.
restaurants.description: Calle Dão pays homage to Havana’s once-thriving El Barrio Chino (Chinatown), once the largest such community in Latin America. As the Cuban and Chinese cultures mixed, a unique fusion of cuisine emerged. The cuisine, cocktails and décor of Calle Dão strive to transport guests back to El Barrio Chino when it was at the height of its existence. Calle Dão has created mouthwatering dishes that seamlessly blend Cuban staples with Asian flavors. The cocktails, created by Mixologist Joy Daniel, also meld the old world with the new using historic names for libations with modern ingredients.

restaurants.summary: Located on Manhattan's Upper East Side, Caravaggio boasts elegant Italian cuisine with a modern twist.
restaurants.description: Located on Manhattan's Upper East Side, Caravaggio boasts elegant Italian cuisine with a modern twist. Its sophisticated cooking, flawless service and exquisite modern setting places it among the top restaurants in the City. Giuseppe Bruno—part of the family behind Italian eatery Sistina—launched this latest venture to carry on the family’s tradition of serving great food to devoted patrons.

restaurants.name: Carlotto
restaurants.summary: Under the leadership of executive chef Andy Kitko and his culinary team, Carlotto’s menu honors Italy’s most celebrated regions.
restaurants.description: Carlotto is an approachable Italian dining experience nestled between Gramercy Park and Union Square, adjacent to its sister restaurant, Oceans. Under the leadership of executive chef Andy Kitko and his culinary team, Carlotto’s menu honors Italy’s most celebrated regions, featuring pastas made daily. Carlotto is set in a modern intimate space designed by the award-winning Rockwell Group, and is anchored by a stunning bar featuring a thoughtfully curated cocktail list and Italian focused wine program.

restaurants.name: Carversteak
restaurants.summary: The menu at Carversteak features a robust steak program, alongside sharable small plates, while the beverage program highlights innovative cocktails inspired by traditional steakhouse flavors.
restaurants.description: Carversteak, the beloved modern steakhouse in Las Vegas from Carver Road Hospitality, opens in Midtown. Spearheaded by CEO Sean Christie and the team behind award-winning Carversteak Las Vegas, Carversteak NYC marks the restaurant’s first national expansion, joining the group’s New York portfolio alongside Rosevale Cocktail Room and Starchild Rooftop. The menu from executive chef Daniel Ontiveros features a robust steak program, alongside sharable small plates. The beverage program from Francesco Lafranconi, Carver Road Hospitality’s vice president of beverage and hospitality culture, highlights innovative cocktails inspired by traditional steakhouse flavors. The space is designed by David Rockwell of Rockwell Group and blends the spirits of historic theater district hangouts with the comfort of a neighborhood bistro.

restaurants.name: Casa Brazilian
restaurants.summary: This charming Tribeca restaurant has been serving up Brazilian home cooking in the West Village since 1998.
restaurants.description: Now located in Tribeca, this charming restaurant has been serving up Brazilian home cooking since 1998 in the West Village. Brazil’s varied geography and rich cultural history are reflected in a diverse menu that includes coastal seafood preparations like Bahian seafood stew, southern churrasco meat dishes such as grilled steak and national favorites like pao de queijo, a savory gluten-free cheese bread. Brazilian expats in the know finish up their meals with the house-made pudim de leite (caramel flan).

restaurants.name: Casa Louie
restaurants.summary: The menu at Hudson Yards' Casa Louie features their homemade pastas and pizzas (including gluten-free pastas and pizza), as well as some traditional Italian dishes.
restaurants.description: Casa Louie—a newer addition to the Hudson Yards area (at the corner of 37th St. and Tenth Ave.)—has quickly become a neighborhood hotspot and go-to restaurant for both locals and visitors. The menu features their homemade pastas and pizzas (including gluten-free pastas and pizza), as well as some traditional Italian dishes. Menu highlights include some unique pizzas, such as pepperoni and jalapeño pizza topped with honey, as well as their most popular Sicilian Square Hot Louie pizza, layered with vodka sauce, house-made mozzarella, and pepperoni, topped off with hot honey, and baked in a pan with a cheese crust. And don't forget to try the tiramisu or soft-serve vanilla gelato made to order.

restaurants.name: Casa Oaxaca
restaurants.summary: Casa Oaxaca is a modern Mexican restaurant inspired by the soul, artistry, and warmth of Oaxaca, reimagined through a contemporary New York lens.
restaurants.description: Casa Oaxaca is a modern Mexican restaurant inspired by the soul, artistry, and warmth of Oaxaca, reimagined through a contemporary New York lens. Rooted in vibrant hospitality and elevated culinary craft, Casa Oaxaca brings together bold regional flavors, handmade masa, smoky chiles, fresh seafood, premium meats and agave-forward cocktails in a lively yet refined setting designed for sharing, celebration, and connection. With warm lighting, rich textures, artisanal details and an energetic atmosphere, it's more than a restaurant—it's a modern Mexican dining experience built around flavor, culture and the pleasure of gathering. The space features two private dining rooms, a plush outdoor patio, and additional outdoor seating for intimate dinners, celebrations, and vibrant downtown evenings.

restaurants.summary: Catch n' Chop, situated on the Upper East Side, is a chef-driven modern American steakhouse with a focus on sustainable, fresh seafood and raw bar.
restaurants.description: Catch n' Chop, situated on the Upper East Side, is a chef-driven modern American steakhouse with a focus on sustainable, fresh seafood and raw bar. Catch n' Chop exudes warmth and welcomes guests with open arms. With its cozy atmosphere, friendly staff, and a menu bursting with mouthwatering dishes, it's the perfect place to unwind and savor a delightful meal. The diverse menu caters to every palate, whether you're looking for a leisurely dinner with loved ones, a quick catch-up with friends, or a solo meal at the bar. Catch n' Chop offers a relaxed setting where laughter flows as freely as the conversation. Come as you are, and leave with a satisfied heart, a full stomach, and a smile.

restaurants.description: A globally influenced seafood restaurant, set in a landmark building in Manhattan’s Meatpacking District, Catch NYC features modern renditions of classic dishes served in a streaming, shareable style of dining. Marrying simple yet elegant seafood, sushi, and steak with excellent service and a lively atmosphere, the 400-seat, tri-level restaurant, complete with al fresco dining on the roof, features signature dishes including the Catch Roll, Truffle Sashimi, A5 Wagyu on a hot rock, Mushroom Spaghetti, and Cantonese Lobster.

restaurants.name: Cha Cha Tang
restaurants.summary: This Chinese restaurant offers a playful rendition of a classic “cha chaan teng” (a Hong Kong-style cafe or diner) with a downtown fine-dining ambiance.
restaurants.description: Cha Cha Tang is a Chinese restaurant by Wilson Tang and John McDonald. The kitchen, led by executive chef Doron Wong, offers a playful rendition of a classic “cha chaan teng” (a Hong Kong-style cafe or diner) with a downtown fine-dining ambiance. The menu features a variety of dim sum, noodles and rice, along with chef specialities. They offer Cantonese Roasted Duck on Friday, Saturday and Sunday, or upon request. The beverage team has curated an extensive wine list along with a collection of Asian Whiskey. Weather permitting, Cha Cha Tang offers al fresco patio dining.

restaurants.name: Chatti by Regi Mathew
restaurants.summary: Chatti by Regi Mathew is New York City's first restaurant entirely dedicated to the toddy shops of Kerala, India.
restaurants.description: Chatti by Regi Mathew is New York City's first restaurant entirely dedicated to the toddy shops of Kerala, India. Chef Regi Mathew, one of India's most celebrated chefs, brings a deep connection to Kerala's culinary heritage, combining meticulous research with award-winning expertise to present the rich and vibrant flavors of his home state. From the seafood-rich backwaters of Alleppey to the hearty meat specialties of the Malabar and High Range regions, both the food and drink menus reflect the many flavors of Kerala and the communal spirit of toddy shop dining. Guests have the option to dine in an expansive dining room, take a seat at the full-service bar, or enter the mezzanine level for private dining. Walk-ins are welcome and reservations can be made via OpenTable.

restaurants.summary: Chito Gvrito's seasonal menu offers classic Georgian flavors with modern twists using locally sourced ingredients paired with natural Georgian wines and craft cocktails.
restaurants.description: Chito Gvrito NYC represents the spirit of the nation of Georgia: sunny, generous and eclectic. Their seasonal menu offers classic Georgian dishes with modern twists using locally sourced ingredients. Discover the vibrant flavors of Georgia, which offer something for everyone—vegetarians will love dishes like Mushroom Khinkali and Georgian Salad, while meat lovers can indulge in Heritage Pork Mtsvadi skewers or Chkmeruli Chicken Tabaka. Similar to Mediterranean flavors, their menu highlights fresh, locally sourced ingredients. Pair your meal with Georgian orange wine or a craft cocktail for a truly unforgettable dining experience.

restaurants.name: Churrascaria Plataforma Brazilian Steakhouse
restaurants.summary: Churrascaria Plataforma Brazilian Steakhouse is a rodízio-style restaurant.
restaurants.description: Churrascaria (choo-rah-scah-ree-ah) is the word for a restaurant that serves meat, mostly grilled, and the rodízio style—serving different cuts of meat—originated in the south of Brazil in the early 1800s. The concept is to serve a wide variety of different cuts of meat, including beef, pork, lamb and chicken, in succession to each diner individually right at their table, thus there is not a traditional menu. Churrascaria Plataforma is the authentic NYC rodízio-style restaurant that features an all-you-can-eat fixed price with continuous table-side service.

This fully functioning winery/wine production facility strives to create wine that contains low to no sulfites while reducing their carbon footprint.

Musical director Daniel Nye hosts the second floor piano lounge nightly, as he did at Bruno Restaurant.

restaurants.name: Coqodaq
restaurants.summary: This "cathedral of fried chicken" skillfully integrates Korean and American influences, featuring dishes cooked by a world-class culinary team, alongside the largest restaurant champagne list in America.
restaurants.description: Coqodaq is an innovative fried chicken concept from Gracious Hospitality Management, designed by Rockwell Group as "the cathedral of fried chicken." They skillfully integrate Korean and American influences, featuring dishes cooked by a world-class culinary team. From certified humane, hormone- and antibiotic-free chicken to gluten-free and anti-inflammatory rice flour batter, and clean cultured oil—every ingredient is of the highest quality and sustainably sourced. The beverage program champions champagne as the pairing of choice, with the largest restaurant champagne list in America, with Blue Chip classics, pages of verticals of vintages, and 100 sparkling wines under $100, breaking down the cost barrier of bubbly. Classic cocktails with an innovative twist, as well as premier beer and wine selections, round out the menu.

restaurants.name: Cosme
restaurants.summary: Mexican inspired rather than straightforward Mexican describes the innovative, vibrant dishes at Enrique Olvera's Cosme.
restaurants.description: Mexican inspired rather than straightforward Mexican describes the innovative, vibrant dishes at Enrique Olvera's Cosme. This Flatiron District venue manages to be both casual and top-drawer thanks to its savvy chef, who trained at the Culinary Institute of America and knows what New Yorkers like. Olvera, who has the critically acclaimed restaurant Pujol in Mexico City plus a few others in Mexico, sources the best chilies, heirloom beans and corn from his native country and looks to local purveyors for meat, fish and seasonal produce. There are roughly 130 seats spread out over the ample bar area and back dining room and a 14-seat private room for parties.

restaurants.name: Crown Shy
restaurants.summary: Find creative fine dining in a stunning art deco tower.
restaurants.description: Crown Shy is the first solo project from the late chef Jamal James Kent. The restaurant, which has one Michelin Star, is located at the base of a landmark art deco tower in Lower Manhattan’s Financial District at 70 Pine Street, its dining room modern and dramatic. Commence with pull-apart olive bread and spellbinding gruyère fritters followed by mafaldine with rock shrimp and chorizo. Other highlights of this creative menu include roasted short rib, crispy eggplant, sungold marinara, and mozzarella. Finish the night with the legendary sticky toffee pudding and green apple sorbet.

restaurants.summary: Wolfgang Puck’s first NYC steakhouse in the Financial District.
restaurants.description: At Cut, acclaimed chef Wolfgang Puck introduces downtown Manhattan to his iconic California cuisine and modern take on the classic steakhouse. The menu boasts top-notch cuts of meat cooked to perfection; the signature Cut burger; sashimi and seafood (for the non-meat eater in your group); and small plates and sides such as mac and cheese, broccolini, bone marrow, suckling pig and pork belly. Cut’s striking decor includes red curtains accented by lightning-bolt-like red neon lights in the bar area; and in the dining room, guests will find a large artwork installation from Alex Israel featuring quotations with fireworks bursting through.

restaurants.description: Da Andrea is a neighborhood Italian ristorante located in Chelsea in Manhattan. Experience the beauty of authentic Italian dining with a menu that specializes in the art of homemade pasta, traditional Italian dishes, delicious risottos, and more. Each dish is meticulously prepared with fresh, locally sourced ingredients and an abundance of experience. Dining is a shared experience and every detail matters. Whether you’re in the mood for a glass of wine or a full four-course meal, Da Andrea takes patrons on a delectable journey in a warm and inviting ambiance.

restaurants.name: David Burke Tavern
restaurants.summary: David Burke Tavern is a modern American tavern on the Upper East Side that features American plates as a reflection of chef Burke’s contemporary approach to cooking, with a nod to elevated New York classics.
restaurants.description: David Burke Tavern is a modern American restaurant situated in a stately townhouse on Manhattan’s Upper East Side. The casual tavern atmosphere of the first floor gives way to sophisticatedly relaxed, clubby rooms on the second. It offers lunch, dinner and brunch, as well as a daily happy hour. The menu features the contemporary American cuisine of which chef/owner David Burke is a much-celebrated pioneer, often accented with his signature playful approach to cooking, with a nod to elevated New York classics, paired with a curated wine list, craft beers and a specialty cocktail program.

restaurants.description: Dear Strangers is a Latin-inspired Modern American restaurant and cocktail bar located in Greenwich Village. Chef Diego Rodriguez oversees the culinary program, while cocktail veterans Bratislav Glisic and Ivan Radulovic oversee the bar program. Reservations are available for dining guests in the 47-seat dining room, while the 12-seat bar is available on a first-come, first-served basis.

restaurants.name: Del Frisco's Grille
restaurants.summary: Located near Radio City and Times Square, Del Frisco's Grille features a sweeping bar with a wood-burning oven, expansive walls showcasing more than 700 bottles of wine and a sprawling patio perfect for al fresco dining.
restaurants.description: Located near Radio City and Times Square, Del Frisco's Grille features a sweeping bar with a wood-burning oven, expansive walls showcasing more than 700 bottles of wine and a sprawling patio perfect for al fresco dining. The modern yet inviting décor is accented with stylish architectural elements and original works of art. The bar buzzes with the energy of the after-work scene, while the dining room provides the perfect setting for guests looking to escape from the rush of the City, meet with a client for a business lunch or dine with friends and family.

restaurants.name: Del Frisco's Grille - Brookfield Place
restaurants.summary: Del Frisco’s features a steakhouse-style menu, with classic starters like a wedge salad and choice cuts of broiled steaks.
restaurants.description: Located in Lower Manhattan’s Brookfield Place, Del Frisco’s features a steakhouse-style menu, with classic starters like a wedge salad and choice cuts of broiled steaks—though you’ll also find variety with ahi tacos, wild mushroom flatbreads, truffled mac and cheese and a cauliflower steak. Meat and seafood meal kits are available, desserts are prepared in house and the wine list is unsurprisingly long.

restaurants.description: Del Frisco's Double Eagle Steakhouse New York is an energetic, sprawling, three-story restaurant in Midtown, featuring floor-to-ceiling windows that offer grand views of Sixth Avenue. Their guests are treated to an unforgettable experience through the chef-driven cuisine, world-class wine program and unparalleled hospitality. Dedicated private dining coordinators will help to plan and personalize your event so you can sit back and relax.

restaurants.name: Delmonico's
restaurants.summary: The classic NYC steakhouse, in business since 1837, is where eggs Benedict and baked Alaska were said to be invented.
restaurants.description: In business since 1837, Delmonico's revolutionized the way we eat out: these guys literally invented eggs Benedict, lobster Newberg and baked Alaska, among other now-standards, and changed the face of fine dining in early America. The financial district location looks exactly like you’d expect from an old-school steak house—deep hues, dark woods and understated opulence in which to enjoy the huge Delmonico rib-eye and the Parmesan creamed spinach.

Located at Essex Market on the Lower East Side of Manhattan, Dhamaka dives deep into the bold, provincial cooking rarely seen outside of Indian homes and roadside stalls. restaurants.name: Dinner Party
restaurants.summary: The cuisine falls somewhere between French, Italian, and, as the chef loves to insist, “Californian”—reflecting the myriad possible directions of a set menu that changes every week.
restaurants.description: Dinner Party was founded in 2021 by six young women with no professional cooking experience and only half-hearted pretensions of sophistication. Most of them were strangers when they started, but they were lifelong friends by the end of the first month open. The restaurant aims to feel that way: like you’re dining among instant friends, laughing as much as you’re eating. The cuisine’s rustic and lovingly-made, balanced but never boring. It falls somewhere between French, Italian, and, as the chef loves to insist, “Californian”—reflecting the myriad possible directions of a set menu that changes every week.

restaurants.summary: Healthy portions of pork ribs, Texas-style brisket and pulled pork, along with plenty of cocktails and seasonal brews, are on the menu at this barbecue spot.
restaurants.description: Long before NYC became a destination for decent ’cue, Dinosaur’s Syracuse, N.Y.-based pit masters rescued the City from infamy with its honky-tonk Harlem branch underneath the Riverside Drive bridge. Done up like a gritty roadhouse, this cavernous meat haven is known for its gut-busting platters of pork ribs, Texas-style brisket and pulled pork. Pick your protein-heavy meal and wash it all down with an ice cold beer from the wide array of artisanal brews.

restaurants.summary: DK PubLIC is a century-old gastropub in Long Island City where history and charm blend seamlessly with a vibrant atmosphere.
restaurants.description: DK PubLIC is a century-old gastropub in Long Island City where history and charm blend seamlessly with a vibrant atmosphere. Step inside and be greeted by the warmth of the wooden bar and the nostalgic appeal of penny tile flooring. Their menu features top-grade comfort food, highlighted by signature dry-aged burgers that are sure to satisfy any craving. Whether you're in the mood for brunch or a late-night bite, DK PubLIC offers something for everyone, including a selection of 12 craft beers on tap to complement your meal. The space is perfect for gatherings, steeped in old-school charm and adorned with vintage decor that invites you to relax and enjoy.

restaurants.name: Docks Off 5th
restaurants.summary: This seafood-centric restaurant, steps away from Radio City Music Hall and Rockefeller Center, offers an unforgettable dining experience with Insta-worthy dishes, drinks and décor.
restaurants.description: Docks Off 5th is a seafood-centric restaurant that is steps away from Radio City Music Hall and Rockefeller Center. Guests can expect an unforgettable dining experience with Instagram-worthy dishes, drinks and décor—as Docks says, "the camera eats first." Try starters like Tuna Won-Tacos (ahi tuna, mango pico, avocado-lime crema) or Lava Shrimp (with creamy spicy volcano sauce). Follow up with an entrée such as Seafood Paradise (jerk salmon and shrimp, knuckle and claw lobster, peppers and onions, pineapple fried rice, open-faced pineapple), Crab Cake Stuffed Salmon (with lemon cream sauce), Filet Oscar (topped with jumbo lump crab meat and hollandaise) or Truffle Filet Frites (8 oz filet mignon, topped with truffle butter, served with shoestring fries or truffle parm fries). Desserts include Pina Colada Crème Brûlée and Fried Oreo Sundae.

restaurants.name: Docks Oyster Bar
restaurants.summary: Docks Oyster Bar has been serving the freshest seafood and oysters for more than 25 years in Midtown Manhattan.
restaurants.description: Docks Oyster Bar has been serving the freshest seafood and oysters for more than 25 years in Midtown Manhattan. They have a large open floor plan with tables lining windows along both Third Avenue and 40th Street, and an expansive bar that serves tasty martinis, wine and cocktails. Docks' daily specials and simply prepared fish are reasons for their longevity, along with an outstanding service team, a great wine list and an amazing New York atmosphere in which guests can create memories.

restaurants.name: Double Knot NYC
restaurants.summary: Double Knot, from restaurateur Michael Schulson, has been celebrated for bold sushi, sashimi and robatayaki, paired with inventive cocktails and saké.
restaurants.description: Since its Philadelphia debut, Double Knot from restaurateur Michael Schulson has been celebrated for bold sushi, sashimi and robatayaki, paired with inventive cocktails and saké. The Midtown Manhattan location offers a bi-level experience that blends lively social energy with focused dining across two thoughtfully designed floors. Upstairs, the sushi bar and cocktail bar set the tone; below, The Amber Room hosts the robatayaki grill and a second bar that carry the same spirit. Together, the two floors offer guests a seamless journey from one experience to the next, while creating a more intimate atmosphere below. Double Knot New York's menu pairs signature dishes like seasonal sashimi and the chef's tasting menu with curated cocktails and saké selections that highlight both classic and inventive flavors. Highlights include hand-cut nigiri, robatayaki-grilled seasonal vegetables, meats and fish, and an array of small plates that showcase the depth of Japanese-inspired cooking with a modern twist.

restaurants.description: DubuHaus is a Korean restaurant centered around authentic handmade dubu (tofu), crafted fresh each morning from organic, non-GMO soybeans. Rooted in Korea's ingredient-first philosophy, the menu features a thoughtful balance of traditional and contemporary Korean dishes designed to highlight the texture, warmth, and seasonality of each ingredient. From comforting stews to fresh seasonal specialties, every dish reflects the restaurant's commitment to everyday nourishment and sincere hospitality. Dine-in reservations, walk-ins, and online ordering are all available.

restaurants.summary: This Lower East Side restaurant offers a fine dining omakase experience that showcases expertly crafted sushi, seasonal ingredients and traditional Japanese techniques.
restaurants.description: EdoYa is a contemporary sushi and omakase restaurant located on Rivington Street in Manhattan's Lower East Side. They offer a fine dining omakase experience that showcases expertly crafted sushi, seasonal ingredients and traditional Japanese techniques. Behind the experience is Chef Edgar, whose more than 25 years of culinary expertise and deep knowledge of Japanese cuisine guide every menu and preparation. Guests can enjoy thoughtfully prepared nigiri, sashimi, and chef-curated tasting menus in an intimate and elegant setting, where freshness, quality and precision are at the heart of every dish.

restaurants.name: Eléa
restaurants.summary: The Upper West Side welcomes a modern split-level Greek restaurant.
restaurants.description: This modern split-level Greek restaurant has a sunny and welcoming atmosphere, with a big bar and plentiful tables. Eléa shares design and menu similarities with Kyma, its downtown sibling. Eggplant-zucchini chips with tzatziki dip and fried piquant kefalograviera cheese are an absolute must. From the raw bar, get yellow fin tuna tartare. Grilled lamb chops and creamy seafood orzotto laced with Metaxa brandy shine among the delicious main courses.

restaurants.description: Pristine Mediterranean-style seafood shines in an industrial-chic Midtown setting at Milos. restaurants.name: Filé Gumbo Bar
restaurants.summary: Beyond the signature gumbo, dining at Filé is an educational feast of the culinary subtleties of Cajun and Creole food.
restaurants.description: Filé Gumbo Bar is inspired by the iconic ingredient used to thicken and flavor their gumbo. The name refers to the dried and ground leaves of the North American sassafras tree—an essential ingredient introduced to the Cajuns by the Choctaw Indians in the 18th century. The centerpiece of the menu is Tiny’s Gumbo, inspired by the owner’s larger-than-life grandfather, Aubrey “Tiny” Gaines, who believed there was nothing better than shellfish and spice. Beyond the signature gumbo, dining at Filé is an educational feast of the culinary subtleties of Cajun and Creole food.

restaurants.name: Fish Cheeks
restaurants.summary: Family-style Thai seafood and great cocktails in NoHo.
restaurants.description: Fish Cheeks has a cheeky design; its awning is layered like colorful fish scales, primary colors brighten the cafeteria-like dining room and overturned baskets serve as lampshades overhead. Brothers and co-chefs Chat and Ohm Suansilphong, whose parents owned a restaurant in Thailand, prepare Thai family-style dishes at varying levels of spiciness; standouts include coconut crab curry and steamed whole fish with aromatic Thai herbs. Non-seafood items like grilled pork cheeks with jeaw sauce and potent cocktails are also exemplary.

restaurants.name: Fish Cheeks Brooklyn
restaurants.summary: Fish Cheeks, a New York City institution since opening in NoHo in 2016, brings their vibrant coastal Thai flavors and warm hospitality to Williamsburg.
restaurants.description: Since opening in NoHo in 2016, Fish Cheeks has become a New York City institution, celebrated for its vibrant coastal Thai flavors and warm hospitality. From the start, it challenged expectations of Thai cuisine in the U.S., moving beyond familiar dishes to highlight the bold, seafood-driven flavors co-founders Jenn Saesue and Chat Suansilphong grew up with. After nearly a decade of loyal followings, constant diner requests, and a "Thai Select" designation recognizing its authenticity and excellence, the brand expanded to Williamsburg, which underscored its impact on shaping New York's understanding of Thai cuisine. Fish Cheeks' flavor-forward cuisine and genuine hospitality have made it a beloved destination for New Yorkers for nearly a decade. The Williamsburg opening extends this spirit to a new neighborhood while preserving everything that defines the flagship. Fish Cheeks continues to evolve while remaining a benchmark for excellence in New York's dining landscape.

restaurants.name: Fogo de Chão Brazilian Steakhouse
restaurants.summary: Fogo de Chão is an authentic Brazilian steakhouse (churrascaria) that has been setting the standard in Brazil since 1979.
restaurants.description: Fogo de Chão is an authentic Brazilian steakhouse (churrascaria) that has been setting the standard in Brazil since 1979. The menu includes delectable cuts of grilled meats such as sizzling steaks, lamb, chicken and pork carved tableside by Brazilian trained gaucho chefs as well as a lighter seafood option. Also offered is a gourmet salad and sides bar consisting of salads, fresh-cut vegetables, cured meats and imported cheeses, as well as a variety of traditional Brazilian side dishes, delectable desserts and award-winning wine list.

restaurants.name: Fogo de Chão Brazilian Steakhouse - Brooklyn
restaurants.summary: This Downtown Brooklyn restaurant features an open churrasco grill giving guests a 360-degree view of gaucho chefs demonstrating the culinary art of churrasco.
restaurants.description: Located at City Point, Downtown Brooklyn’s largest entertainment, shopping, and dining destination, this restaurant features an open churrasco grill giving guests a 360-degree view of gaucho chefs demonstrating the culinary art of churrasco as they butcher, prepare and grill high-quality cuts of meat over an open flame. The restaurant's warm, timeless, approachable setting compliments the local Brooklyn community. Highlights include an expansive dining room centered around a white Carrera marble Market Table anchored at the front of the grill, dry aged meat lockers for in-house aging, and a lively indoor bar, ideal for all-day happy hour.

restaurants.name: Fogo de Chão Brazilian Steakhouse - World Trade Center
restaurants.summary: Fogo de Chão's seventh New York restaurant, located at Westfield World Trade Center, features an open churrasco grill where guests can dine and watch gaucho chefs demonstrate the culinary art of churrasco.
restaurants.description: Fogo de Chão's seventh New York restaurant is located on the corner of Church Street and Cortlandt Way at Westfield World Trade Center, a premier destination for shopping. Fogo de Chão Brazilian Steakhouse - World Trade Center features an open churrasco grill where guests can dine and watch gaucho chefs demonstrate the culinary art of churrasco as they butcher, prepare and grill different cuts of meat over an open flame. The main dining room is anchored by a white Carrara Market Table and their signature bas-relief interpretation of Antonio Carigni’s O Lacador statue, the embodiment of the gaucho culture. The restaurant also features soaring wine displays, dry aged meat lockers for in-house aging and a lively indoor bar, ideal for all-day happy hour.

restaurants.name: Folk
restaurants.summary: This new addition to Park Slope offers chef Jay Kumar’s cooking, known for blending cultures, à la carte, along with a unique cocktail program, thoughtfully curated to complement Indian flavors.
restaurants.description: Founded by chef Jay Kumar of Lore, Folk is a neighborhood restaurant inspired by community spirit. The new addition to Park Slope offers Chef Kumar’s cooking, known for blending cultures, à la carte, along with a unique cocktail program, thoughtfully curated to complement Indian flavors. Guests have the option of sitting at the sleek marble bar, the cozy booth-lined tables below oversized windows, and quiet hightop seating. Walk-ins are accepted at all three, but reservations are encouraged for the tables (available on Resy).

French Louie is open for brunch, weekday lunch and dinner.

Natural wines dominate the list, with by-the-glass options poured from magnums and jeroboams.

restaurants.description: Williamsburg’s Fushimi has striking glossy decor, an appropriate setting for its fusion of traditional Japanese sushi and sashimi with modern French accents. Fushimi aims to produce visionary Japanese-fusion dishes, using the highest quality ingredients and state-of-the-art methods. Hand-picked, fresh ingredients from local farms are shipped weekly to their location and are artistically handled by our expert chefs. The restaurant flaunts its exceptional menu, premium service, and its trendy ambiance and nightlife, making it a must-go. Fushimi welcomes customers looking for innovative developments of traditional cuisines, Japanese food lovers, or simply anyone wanting to try something new.

restaurants.name: Gage & Tollner
restaurants.summary: Gage & Tollner, opened in 1879, is the oldest landmark restaurant in New York, featuring Victorian decor and working gas lamps.
restaurants.description: Gage & Tollner, opened in 1879, is the oldest landmark restaurant in New York, featuring Victorian decor and working gas lamps. With three longtime friends and celebrated local restaurateurs at the helm—partners Sohui Kim (chef, Insa/The Good Fork), Ben Schneider (Insa/The Good Fork), and St. John Frizell (Fort Defiance)—a community-driven team is restoring Gage & Tollner to its former glory and guiding it into the 21st century. Inspiration for the food and beverage offerings come from the Gage & Tollner archives, honoring and elevating beloved longtime classics with meticulously-sourced ingredients and diligent technique.

restaurants.name: Gallaghers Steakhouse
restaurants.summary: Back in the prohibition years, Gallaghers Steakhouse served as a speakeasy.
restaurants.description: Back in the prohibition years, Gallaghers Steakhouse served as a speakeasy. Now, 80 years later, this signature New York establishment is a prime spot for a genuine steak. The restaurant’s meat-aging room is stocked with USDA Prime dry-aged beef, which is sure to bring a tear to the eye of any carnivore. The dinner menu features chicken, seafood and even a veggie plate, but the steak is where it’s at.

restaurants.name: Gaonnuri
restaurants.summary: Gaonnuri's 39th floor penthouse in Koreatown affords wraparound views of Midtown.
restaurants.description: Gaonnuri boasts one of the most spectacular locations of any Korean restaurant in the City, occupying a 39th floor penthouse in Koreatown that affords wraparound views of Midtown. With a capacity of 300, and two private spaces that fit 40 each, it's a great place for business and social events. There is Seoul sophistication in the menu, which includes beef tartare marinated in sesame oil and soy sauce, seafood-and-scallion pancake, braised short ribs and spicy codfish stew. The bar/lounge, which offers views of the Empire State Building, emphasizes the vodka-like soju, but there's also an extensive wine list designed to match the Korean food.

restaurants.description: For a taste of Italy in Brooklyn's Coney Island, look no further than Gargiulo’s, an authentic Italian restaurant serving delicious, traditional Neapolitan fare made from family recipes that have stood the test of time. Their food is made with fresh, high-quality ingredients and cooked in-house with care. Gargiulo’s has been family-owned and operated since 1907, making them a Brooklyn staple and a Coney Island favorite for over 100 years.

restaurants.name: Ginger Ristoranti
restaurants.summary: Guided by the principles of the world’s Blue Zones—regions where vitality and longevity flourish—Ginger Ristoranti New York's cuisine is ingredient-driven, plant-forward, and rooted in refined simplicity.
restaurants.description: Ginger Ristoranti New York is a reference point for those who choose a healthy and balanced Mediterranean diet. It's the right place for those who want a full and energetic breakfast, a tasty but light snack, a refined lunch or dinner. Their menus evolve with the rhythm of the seasons, celebrating ingredients that are thoughtfully sourced, organically grown, and prepared with a sense of harmony and purpose. Guided by the principles of the world’s Blue Zones—regions where vitality and longevity flourish—Ginger Ristoranti's cuisine is ingredient-driven, plant-forward, and rooted in refined simplicity. From breakfast through to the evening aperitivo, each dish is crafted with precision and purpose, embodying freshness, harmony and authenticity. This is Italian cuisine as it was meant to be: quietly wholesome, profoundly flavorful, and always a timeless pleasure.

restaurants.summary: Gran Morsi, named after the Italian word for "bites" epitomizes elegant simplicity.
restaurants.description: Gran Morsi, named after the Italian word for “bites,” epitomizes elegant simplicity. This airy and convivial TriBeCa restaurant, on the border of the Financial District, specializes in boldly flavored Italian fare with a strong focus on small and shared plates, many of which are cooked in the brick oven. Gran Morsi provides downtown Manhattan residents and visitors with a dining experience fit for whatever they’re in the mood for, whether it’s a special occasion celebration, an intimate evening or a casual night out with friends. Gran Morsi also has a private event space perfect for any and all special occasions.

restaurants.description: The landmark Vanderbilt Hall, once Grand Central Terminal’s main waiting room, has been transformed into Grand Brasserie, a New York City meeting place with Parisian flair. The brasserie, open daily from 5:30am to 2:00am, is an airy 400-seat destination, featuring two impressive bars and dining rooms, offering a menu filled with timeless French classics. Whether you’re seeking a morning espresso, a leisurely lunch, or a late-night drink, Grand Brasserie is a go-to destination for authentic French cuisine in Manhattan's Midtown East.

Grandma’s Home has popular locations throughout China, and their first American restaurant brings the same casual approach to regional Chinese cuisine stateside, with this new location in the centrally-located Flatiron District neighborhood of Manhattan.

The brick-lined wine cellar room is particularly lovely and great for large private parties.

restaurants.name: Gui Steakhouse
restaurants.summary: Gui Steakhouse is elevated steakhouse experience that integrates the unique flavors and techniques of Korean beef grilling.
restaurants.description: The team behind Gui Steakhouse wanted to create an elevated steakhouse experience by integrating the unique flavors and techniques of Korean beef grilling. Unlike traditional steak preparation, the Korean method highlights diverse charms and tastes, which they've modernized to bring a distinctive twist to the classic steakhouse concept. This Times Square restaurant takes pride in the quality of their premium steaks, which stems from two main partnerships that ensure they always have access to exceptional beef. These partnerships are carefully selected based on their commitment to sustainable farming methods and superior animal husbandry: Creekstone Farms is committed to excellence, combining superior Black Angus and Duroc genetics, top-tier livestock management, and advanced processing; and Pat LaFrieda Meat Purveyors has delivered butchery excellence for 100 years, sourcing premium meats from small domestic farms, offering all-natural, organic, and grass-fed options.

restaurants.name: Haidilao Huoguo
restaurants.summary: This reliable hot pot chain restaurant is open all day and night.
restaurants.description: The Flushing outpost of this famous Chinese chain is beloved for its great service and late hours—it’s open until at least 4am every day. The premise of hot pot is simple: pick a broth; order proteins, vegetables and carbs; cook everything in the broth yourself, and then dip each piece into the sauce of your choice. It’s a marathon of a meal, best enjoyed with a group that can linger around the table together. Make a reservation ahead of time.

restaurants.name: Hanaya Omakase
restaurants.summary: Chef Yousi Chen serves a 13-course Omakase at his Chef's Counter with an à la carte menu as well.
restaurants.description: Hanaya is chef Yousi Chen's newest venture. After years of experience with sushi legends such as Chef Nakazawa and Chef Nakajima, Chef Yousi has brought an approachable Omakase option to the Hell's Kitchen neighborhood of Manhattan. Chef Yousi serves a 12-course Omakase at his Chef's Counter with an à la carte menu as well. With ingredients sourced from Toyosu Market, the omakase offered at Hanaya offers the season's best ingredients in a carefully curated tasting course. Start with fresh, seasonal bites that lead into an elevated nigiri selection. Chef Yousi has his fish flown in multiple times a week to ensure outstanding quality. Hanaya is open for service from Tuesday through Sunday.

restaurants.name: Hard Rock Cafe
restaurants.summary: As continually mobbed as the Beatles at Shea, the Hard Rock Café is an ongoing international phenomenon.
restaurants.description: As continually mobbed as the Beatles at Shea, the Hard Rock Café is an ongoing international phenomenon. Waits are common and the volume is up to 11, but the burger and bar-style snacks are hard to resist. Rock and roll memorabilia covers every square inch—remember that Elvis, Led Zeppelin and the Beatles are watching over your every bite.

restaurants.name: Hav & Mar
restaurants.summary: Hav & Mar is a vibrant seafood house in Chelsea from chef Marcus Samuelsson.
restaurants.description: Hav & Mar is a vibrant seafood house from chef Marcus Samuelsson located in the Manhattan arts district of Chelsea. The stunning dining room and dazzling bar, a mix of contemporary and classical design, features original work by award-winning artist Derrick Adams. Chef Samuelsson and executive chef Fariyal Abdullahi’s energetic and globally inspired menu focuses on thoughtfully sourced seafood and seasonal greenmarket produce. Gracious hospitality, show-stopping cocktails, and a groundbreaking wine list spotlighting BIPOC and female producers contribute to Hav & Mar’s convivial and festive atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Havana Central
restaurants.summary: Through its festive ambiance, vibrant décor and mouth-watering food, dining at Havana Central is like taking a mini vacation.
restaurants.description: Havana Central evokes the 1950s golden era of Cuba, capturing Havana’s heyday as the world’s most tantalizing playground. Through its festive ambiance, vibrant décor and mouth-watering food, dining at Havana Central is like taking a mini vacation. Traditional dishes like vaca frita, ropa vieja and arroz con pollo are a celebration of Cuban cuisine, and the cocktail list includes some of the best mojitos and sangrias in New York.

restaurants.name: Hawksmoor
restaurants.summary: The goal of this steakhouse is to serve the perfect steak in an environment where everyone, guests and staff, can relax and enjoy themselves.
restaurants.description: Hawksmoor was inspired by a labor of love to find the best possible beef and perfect the seemingly simple art of cooking steak. The menu revolves around all-natural beef from family-run farms, many based in upstate New York, Pennsylvania, and New England, simply seasoned with flaked sea salt and seared over live-fire charcoal. Hawksmoor's home, near Gramercy Park in the historic United Charities Building—which was closed from public view for over a century—boasts a 26-foot vaulted ceiling, a 35-seat bar, and two private dining spaces.
