restaurants.name: Hearth
restaurants.summary: Hearth is everything its name implies...a warm, comfortable restaurant with hospitality as its goal.
restaurants.description: Hearth is the East Village restaurant from chef Marco Canora, recipient of the James Beard Award for Best Chef New York City, 2017. Chef Canora’s cuisine, with a warm nod to Tuscany, employs seasonal, locally-sourced ingredients that taste delicious and make you feel good. The intimate restaurant spaces provide the perfect backdrop for cozy first dates, celebratory family gatherings, and refined business experiences. The Hearth wine cellar features smaller, independent producers, and a bounty of organic, natural, and biodynamic bottles.

Henry's End features a seasonal menu highlighted by their annual Wild Game Festival in the fall and winter.

restaurants.description: Heritage Grand Bakery Restaurant & Pizza Bar is located near Bryant Park and the New York Public Library. Inspired by the Mediterranean, they serve signature breads, pastries and wood-fired pizzas in a stylish and worldly setting. The Grand Bar features classy cocktails and a refined assortment of wine and beer. The open kitchen, open mixing room, and pizzaiolo-manned pizza ovens offer customers a glimpse into the restaurant's operation. The retail bakery sells freshly baked breads, pastries, viennoiseries, grab and go breakfast items, hot and cold lunch sandwiches, salads as well as premium coffee and teas.

restaurants.name: Hudson VU
restaurants.summary: Hudson VU, perched atop the Ink 48 Hotel in Hell’s Kitchen, presents a sophisticated and elevated take on New York rooftop dining.
restaurants.description: Hudson VU, perched atop the Ink 48 Hotel in Hell’s Kitchen, presents a sophisticated and elevated take on New York rooftop dining. The menu highlights creative culinary bites and modern twists on classic flavors, all designed to complement a master-class cocktail program and a carefully curated selection of spirits. Guests can enjoy their experience against the backdrop of sweeping, unobstructed views of the Hudson River and the Manhattan skyline, whether relaxing in the stylish outdoor space or settling into the sleek, modern interior. With its vibrant pulse and stunning sunset vistas, Hudson VU offers a flavor-forward escape that captures the distinctive character of the City from high above.

restaurants.summary: The team at ilili invites guests to experience the heart of Lebanese, Mediterranean, and Middle Eastern hospitality, right in the vibrant Midtown East neighborhood of Manhattan.
restaurants.description: The team at ilili invites guests to experience the heart of Lebanese, Mediterranean, and Middle Eastern hospitality, right in the vibrant Midtown East neighborhood of Manhattan. Whether you’re there for a memorable meal or or hosting a private event, ilili Midtown is a celebration of heritage, innovation, and the unforgettable tastes of Lebanon and the Mediterranean. ilili is an extension of three generations of Massoud family stories. These stories are enriched in joy, loss, struggle, resilience and 100 years of outstanding hospitality, making their establishment historic while creating new beginnings. Chef Philippe Massoud’s concept was simple: to revive and bring this ancient cuisine to a public who hadn’t properly experienced it.

restaurants.description: Indian Table pays homage to the food, art and culture of India in Brooklyn’s Cobble Hill neighborhood. Indian Table showcases the flavors, herbs, spices and cooking techniques of Goa, the coastal Indian state once colonized by the Portuguese, with a distinct British influence. The menu is inspired by executive chef Eric McCarthy, who grew up in the Goan village of Candolim and led the kitchens of acclaimed NYC restaurants Tamarind, Tulsi and Brick Lane Curry House.

menu.text:
It took two years of hard work and passion for Chef Eric to turn Indian
Table into a full-fledged Goa cuisine restaurant that diners have accepted.


That did not stop Chef Eric from digging deeper into the culinary history of
his home state of Goa.


After two trips to his home state of Goa following the pandemic, Chef Eric
is now pushing the boundaries to present dishes that directly connect with
and draw influence from the Portuguese colonial era. While a part of Goan
cuisine was lost over time
as cuisines from other states became the norm to accommodate the influx of
tourists, and some that were lost via a generational gap.


For winter Restaurant Week 2026, chef Eric presents "GOAN JOVHAN,"
which is a blend of classic Portuguese-Goan dishes paired with traditional
Goan home-style cooking in a three-course dining spread that includes an
appetizer course, an entree course served in a traditional platter with
various condiments and sides, and a dessert course. Also available is a special
cocktail and a mocktail menu for your pairing.

restaurants.name: Indochine
restaurants.summary: French-Vietnamese cuisine is served in this perennial hot spot.
restaurants.description: It opened its doors more than 30 years ago, and Indochine still holds onto the elements that made it famous, including a crowd of yuppies mixed with the fashion world and on-the-rise celebrities. Utilizing exotic-meets-tropical design elements such as Japanese box lights, palm trees painted onto the walls and a sleek tiled floor worked in the late ’80s for this French-Vietnamese fusion restaurant, so why change now? Some consider Indochine to be past its prime, but revelers still frequent this pioneer for the consistent spring rolls, the reliable sole steamed in a banana leaf and the glazed duck breast.

restaurants.name: Ishq
restaurants.summary: The menu at this East Village restaurant is a celebration of India's culinary treasures—from aromatic curries to flavorful tandoori offerings, all made with the finest spices and ingredients.
restaurants.description: The menu at this East Village restaurant is a celebration of India's culinary treasures—from aromatic curries to flavorful tandoori offerings, all made with the finest spices and ingredients. But what truly sets Ishq apart is its dedication to storytelling through food. Every dish on the menu is a tribute to ancestors, rekindling the love for age-old recipes while adapting to the global palate of New York City diners. At Ishq, tradition meets innovation on every plate. The dishes are steeped in authenticity, drawing from the rich culinary heritage of India’s diverse regions. Each recipe has been meticulously crafted to preserve its original flavors, yet plated with an artistic flair that speaks to modern sensibilities.

restaurants.name: Izakaya Futago
restaurants.summary: Discover playful innovations like Spoon Sushi, a one-bite reimagining of traditional nigiri sushi, alongside freshly-made soba noodles, izakaya dishes, and original cocktails crafted with sake.
restaurants.description: At Izakaya Futago in East Midtown Manhattan, New Yorkers can discover playful innovations like Spoon Sushi: a one-bite reimagining of traditional nigiri sushi. Each skewer is carefully prepared and grilled to perfection. Enjoy the savory aroma and juicy flavor, along with the live cooking experience at the counter. The menu also features handcrafted, freshly-made soba noodles (Ni-Hachi buckwheat noodles) together with an extensive selection of izakaya dishes. Enjoy original cocktails crafted with sake, richly flavored Japanese whisky, and authentic Japanese bar food prepared by their skilled Japanese chef—whether it’s a romantic date, a gathering with friends, a quiet moment alone, or a drink with colleagues after work, guests will feel at home at the bar.

restaurants.name: Jack's All Day
restaurants.summary: This casual American restaurant, in the Theatre District at the corner of Restaurant Row, spotlights classic American comfort food done right, alongside a thoughtfully crafted cocktail program.
restaurants.description: Jack's All Day is a casual American restaurant from Friedman's Hospitality Group, located in the Theatre District at 46th Street and Eighth Avenue, at the corner of Restaurant Row. The menu spotlights classic American comfort food done right—from great burgers and chops to house-made meatloaf—alongside a thoughtfully crafted cocktail program featuring house-made creations. The lively dining room makes it a natural fit for a pre-theater bite or a relaxed dinner with friends.

restaurants.description: Pickles are more than just a garnish at this Southern-inspired eatery; they’re a way of life. Diners can partake of the spot’s many different pickled veggies, from your standard kosher dills to pickled green beans and beets. Those not in a briny state of mind can opt for neo-Southern grub including sausages made from humanely raised beef, and shrimp and bacon grits and biscuits crafted from sustainable ingredients.

restaurants.description: Nestled into a cobblestone square next to a Long Island Railroad station, Jade Eatery & Lounge's address hints at why it's said to be "Forest Hills' hidden gem." The space integrates a zen-like atmosphere with inspirational quotes that adorn the walls, a serene koi pond, and a large Buddha statue smiling benevolently on guests guiding them to a choice entree. Jade serves favorite Pan-Asian and southeast Asian dishes, as well as creative culinary innovations that have become neighborhood favorites, including signature dishes like Sushi Pizza and Calcutta Chicken.

restaurants.name: Jade Rabbit
restaurants.summary: Jade Rabbit is a lush and lively rooftop izakaya and cocktail bar atop the Kimpton Era Midtown New York that features small plates bursting with Asian flavors, along with flavorful riffs on Asian and tiki cocktails.
restaurants.description: Named after the mythical jade rabbit of the moon, Jade Rabbit is a lush and lively rooftop izakaya and cocktail bar atop the Kimpton Era Midtown New York that features small plates bursting with Asian flavors, along with flavorful riffs on Asian and tiki cocktails. It offers sweeping views of the Empire State Building, Rockefeller Center and the NYC skyline. Drawing on New York’s Chinatown dining legacies, its tomato-red bar is framed by tiled portals and temple-like joinery, grounded in intimacy by hand-painted lotus motifs. The rooftop izakaya offering vibrant, shareable small plates inspired by Asian flavors, including lobster dumplings with Maine lobster, and a spicy tuna hand roll made with bluefin tuna. As the night unfolds, so do the drinks—bright, effervescent, and quietly complex—each cocktail is crafted to capture the moment.

restaurants.name: Jazba
restaurants.summary: Jazba is a tribute and celebration of India's famous eateries—their take on some of the iconic dishes which are more than a century old.
restaurants.description: Jazba is a vibrant new East Village restaurant from the team behind the trailblazing Flatiron District Indian restaurant, Junoon. Jazba is a tribute and celebration of India's famous eateries—their take on some of the iconic dishes which are more than a century old. These diverse eateries, integral to India’s culinary identity, typically serve a single specialty dish until sold out for the day. Jazba's menu is inspired by the soul and diversity of these eateries’ strong connection to the roots that run deep across the country, bringing India’s beloved everyday dining culture to the East Village.

restaurants.name: JoJo
restaurants.summary: A lavishly gorgeous and perfectly refined town house is home to one of Jean-Georges Vongerichten's greatest dining accomplishments.
restaurants.description: Jean-Georges Vongeritchen’s first restaurant, established in 1991 and named after the childhood nickname his mother would call him, is situated in a duplex townhouse on the Upper East Side. With a modern and fresh design, JoJo maintains an understated, warm and friendly atmosphere. It’s a simple and casual neighborhood restaurant serving a farm-to-table menu with mostly organic, local ingredients.

restaurants.name: Junoon
restaurants.summary: Junoon's name, meaning "passion" or "obsession," is an indication of the dedication that went into this restaurant.
restaurants.description: "Junoon" is an Urdu word, also frequently used in Hindi, meaning "passion" or "obsession," and it's an indication of the dedication that went into this restaurant. In addition to the 100-seat restaurant is a 45-seat private dining area and a 50-seat cocktail bar and lounge. The refined menu covers all the bases of Indian cooking, from tandoor to cast-iron and open-fire-pit cooking to stone-searing. Highlights include lobster tandoori, Cornish hen with pomegranate and roasted cumin, and lamb shoulder with papaya juice and garam masala. Other unusual touches for an Indian restaurant: organic, sustainably raised ingredients and an impressive wine list.

restaurants.name: Kashkaval Garden
restaurants.summary: Kashkaval Garden offers a casual, relaxed environment in which to enjoy wines, cocktails and Mediterranean food in Hell's Kitchen.
restaurants.description: Kashkaval Garden offers a casual, relaxed, and rustic environment in which to enjoy wines, cocktails and Mediterranean-inspired food in Hell's Kitchen. Appetizers include homemade tapas with hot pita; grilled halloumi cheese sticks served with tomato-harissa dipping sauce; peppadews, spicy-sweet peppers stuffed with feta and mint or goat cheese and basil; and kale salad with figs and Pecorino. Move on to fondues made with Bulgarian Kashkaval cheese, classic gruyère, and truffle. Enjoy skewers of marinated chicken, lamb kofte, salmon in grape leaves, grilled vegetables, “Impossible” meatballs or grilled octopus. Finish things off with baklava or a chocolate torte.

restaurants.name: Kings of Kobe
restaurants.summary: The towering American Wagyu burger creations and mouth-melting American Wagyu steaks—and the frenzy of sides—speak to the Kings of Kobe core: unadulterated, delicious fun.
restaurants.description: Known for its wildly creative, premium American Wagyu burgers, Kings of Kobe takes everything up a notch with bold flavors, indulgent ingredients, and a touch of irreverence. But the story doesn’t stop at the bun: their American Wagyu steaks bring the same swagger, seared hot and paired with house-made sauces that hit hard. For those looking for the ultimate indulgence, they offer a selection of Japanese A5 Wagyu—rich, rare, and priced like nowhere else in NYC. Kings of Kobe is open seven days a week for lunch and dinner, with a daily Happy Hour, and an all-day bar dining menu, to deliver steakhouse-level firepower in a space that’s more fun than formal. Guests rave about the energy, friendly service, and inventive starters like giant mozzarella sticks, Wagyu “cinnamon buns,” and other sleeper hits that go way beyond beef. Whether you’re diving into cocktails at the bar or going all-in on Wagyu, the portions are big, the vibe is bigger, and the flavor is loud, proud, and unapologetically Wagyu.

restaurants.name: La Boca
restaurants.summary: Celebrating the layered heritage of Argentine cuisine, La Boca at Faena by Francis Mallmann brings together bold tradition, soulful technique and a deep reverence for simplicity.
restaurants.description: Celebrating the layered heritage of Argentine cuisine, La Boca at Faena by Francis Mallmann brings together bold tradition, soulful technique and a deep reverence for simplicity. The menu, which honors the flavors of his beloved Buenos Aires neighborhood, blends Spanish, Italian, and Patagonian influences through Mallmann’s elemental approach. Within a richly textured space, alive with curated art, storm-lit chandeliers, and nightly music, La Boca invites guests to slow down, savor, and step into a world where every detail is touched by memory, myth, and meaning. The dress code is "smart, elegant attire, appropriate for the upscale atmosphere," and jackets are recommended but not required.

restaurants.description: La Fleur Rouge, a unique culinary experience rooted in Brooklyn, merges the vibrant flavors of Chinese cuisine with French culinary finesse, helmed by a Michelin-trained chef. Indulge in seasonal dishes that showcase a masterful fusion of Eastern and Western gastronomy. The curated wine list, meticulously crafted by a sommelier, features an exquisite selection of French vintages from Burgundy, Bordeaux, and the Rhône Valley. Additionally, the unique cocktail menu draws inspiration from both cultures, presenting a delightful alchemy of flavors. In a warm and inviting ambiance, the focus on high-quality ingredients, expert service, and exceptional beverages promises an unforgettable journey for all who enter.

restaurants.name: La Marchande
restaurants.summary: La Marchande is chef John Fraser’s modernized take on the French brasserie, set in The Wall Street Hotel.
restaurants.description: La Marchande is chef John Fraser’s modernized take on the French brasserie. Set in The Wall Street Hotel, La Marchande nods to the history of the rusticated beaux-arts building that was once the site of the original 18th-century stock exchange. The menu, co-developed by Fraser and executive chef Rick Horiike, reflects the sultry classics of French brasserie cuisine, reimagined by a global pantry. Signature dishes, such as grilled lobster with coconut sauce-américaine, steamed Dover sole with vermouth-lime butter, and lamb prime rib, are modernized and lightened by unique, global seasoning.

restaurants.summary: Masseria means farmhouse in Italian, and this restaurant’s inspiration is evident in the stone walls and exposed wooden beams.
restaurants.description: Masseria means farmhouse in Italian, and this restaurant’s inspiration is evident in the stone walls and exposed wooden beams. La Masseria is close to Broadway, making it an ideal pre-theater dining alternative to Times Square’s chain restaurants. Warm and inviting, this West Side jewel serves scrumptious dishes from the Puglia region in Italy. A large assortment of entrees satisfies the pasta-lover, the carnivore and the vegetarian alike.

restaurants.name: La Pecora Bianca Bryant Park
restaurants.summary: La Pecora Bianca Bryant Park offers a relaxed, all-day dining experience with approachable, quality Italian food, in a stylish and comfortable setting.
restaurants.description: La Pecora Bianca Bryant Park offers a relaxed, all-day dining experience with approachable, quality Italian food, in a stylish and comfortable setting. They take Italian food back to its roots as a local and seasonal cuisine, with a menu that centers around house-made pastas and modern takes on classic Italian fare. All of La Pecora Bianca's pastas, including their signature rigatoni vodka, gramigna, and tagliatelle bolognese, are made daily in-house. Their drinks are inspired by the tradition of aperitivo hour on the ‘Piazza,’ and feature the La Pecora Rosa organic rosé, an extensive selection of spritzes and negronis, and signature cocktails built around Italian Amari.

restaurants.summary: La Piazza New York is an elegant Italian restaurant in Midtown Manhattan that channels two decades of Venetian culinary tradition into New York City.

Hand-rolled pastas, fresh Adriatic seafood, and premium cuts are paired with a curated wine list and craft cocktails, all served in a modern dining room.

restaurants.name: La Sirene
restaurants.summary: The menu at La Sirène is crafted to reflect the best of South France and the freshest ingredients of the season.
restaurants.description: Chef/owner Didier Pawlicki lived in the hotel of his parents in the Pyrenees Mountains in France from the age of 6 to 16, when he left to attend the French Culinary School in Toulouse. His menu at La Sirène is crafted to reflect the best of South France and the freshest ingredients of the season. The restaurant's focus is on French Southern homemade styles and quality ingredients (Cuisine Bourgeoise) paired with a respectable wine list and friendly, professional service.

restaurants.name: La Tête d’Or
restaurants.summary: La Tête d’Or is chef Daniel Boulud's New York steakhouse, which brings together the essence of American tradition with a refined French flair.
restaurants.description: La Tête d’Or is a New York steakhouse bringing together the essence of American tradition with a refined French flair. The first steakhouse of renowned chef Daniel Boulud, it features a richly enticing menu that offers all the indulgence of steakhouse favorites, elevated by the most premium cuts of meat and seafood offerings, plus the chef's specialty: perfectly flavorful sauces. Designed by David Rockwell, the restaurant's grand yet welcoming decor features soaring ceilings, deep blue banquettes, and warm wood and copper accents. This thoughtfully crafted ambiance provides a perfect backdrop for celebrating timeless elegance and chef Boulud's culinary artistry.

restaurants.summary: Lalyn is a modern Thai restaurant in Manhattan's Garment District that's known for authentic Thai food with a refined touch and Thai-inspired cocktails, wine and craft beverages.
restaurants.description: Lalyn is a modern Thai restaurant in Manhattan's Garment District, near Midtown, Times Square, and Herald Square. Known for authentic Thai food with a refined touch, Lalyn offers classic dishes like Pad Thai, curries, and fried rice alongside regional specialties, all made with premium ingredients, house-made curry pastes and fresh Thai herbs. Enjoy Thai-inspired cocktails, wine and craft beverages with flavors like lemongrass, pandan and kaffir lime. With a calm, upscale, spa-like atmosphere, Lalyn is ideal for lunch, dinner, date nights, group dining and private events—bringing elevated Thai dining and genuine Thai hospitality to Manhattan.

restaurants.name: Langan's
restaurants.summary: Whether you're enjoying a perfectly mixed cocktail, savoring delicious food, or simply soaking in the lively ambiance, Langan’s continues to be a cornerstone of the City’s vibrant nightlife scene.
restaurants.description: Langan’s is a beloved old neighborhood favorite that recently reopened on 47th Street in Midtown Manhattan after closing in 2018. For 25 years, the original Langan’s was a legendary gathering spot, attracting a diverse and eclectic crowd, from celebrities to political figures to cultural icons like Meryl Streep, Alec Baldwin, Senator John McCain, and Johnny Rotten. Journalists, media personalities, and locals alike flocked to the bar, drawn by its warm, welcoming atmosphere and rich history. The newly reopened Langan’s honors its storied past while offering a fresh, contemporary setting. Known for its warm Irish hospitality, the bar features an open-plan, grand horseshoe wraparound bar that invites conversation and connection. With a large liquor selection and a menu of fabulous crafted cocktails, Langan’s offers both traditional and inventive drinks to satisfy every palate. The bar also boasts an upscale New American menu that elevates comfort food with refined twists.

restaurants.summary: Set in a romantic and welcoming Restaurant Row townhouse, Lattanzi is celebrated for its "Roman Jewish-style specialties.
restaurants.description: Opened in 1984, Lattanzi Cucina Italiana is a fine dining Italian restaurant set in a romantic and welcoming Restaurant Row townhouse. Lattanzi is celebrated for its "Roman Jewish-style specialties," and is ideal for both the pre-theater and post-theater crowd. Owned and operated by the Lattanzi family, the restaurant has been recognized as one of the City's finest. Executive chef Paolo Lattanzi's kitchen produces authentic Italian cuisine, such as their signature carciofi alla giudia—artichokes deep-fried in olive oil and garlic—a guest favorite.

restaurants.name: Laut
restaurants.summary: Laut presents the best recipes, dishes and flavors from South East Asia, preserving the flavor profiles of each dish while maintaining the integrity of each cuisine.
restaurants.description: Laut, located at Union Square, was one of the first Malaysian restaurants to receive a Michelin Star in NYC. They focus on presenting the best recipes, dishes and flavors from South East Asia, with a goal of preserving the flavor profiles of each dish while maintaining the integrity of each cuisine. The only way to achieve that is to recreate them from scratch with regionally authentic spices and the freshest ingredients. Take an adventuruous journey through their menu, which ranges from local favorites, street foods, different curries, spicy and sour broths, satays, noodles, bread (roti), and rice dishes.

restaurants.name: Le B.
restaurants.summary: Tableside presentations, intricate flavors, and forgotten pleasures mined from the history books are hallmarks of Le B.’s ethos.
restaurants.description: Le B. is a stylish, supper-club setting, taking inspiration from a 100-year history in Lower Manhattan. With a Continental menu interpreted for the modern diner, the cuisine celebrates all animals from the land and sea. Set in a jewel-like dining room, Le B. channels the energy and joie de vivre of Angie Mar’s beloved, cult favorite restaurant, The Beatrice Inn, while showcasing her unwavering dedication to technique and hospitality. Tableside presentations, intricate flavors, and forgotten pleasures mined from the history books are hallmarks of Le B.’s ethos, filtered through the lens of modern-day downtown NYC.

restaurants.name: Le Gratin
restaurants.summary: Le Gratin echoes the traditional bistros and bouchons of chef Daniel Boulud's hometown of Lyon, France, known for their welcoming ambiance and soulful cuisine.
restaurants.description: Located in the Financial District, Le Gratin echoes the traditional bistros and bouchons of chef Daniel Boulud's hometown of Lyon, France, known for their welcoming ambiance and soulful cuisine. The rustic menu reflects a soulful approach to seasonality, bright flavors, and classic techniques highlighting special ingredients from local purveyors. Lyonnais classics such as “Quenelle de Brochet au Gratin” and “Steak Tartare à la Parisienne” share space with seasonal dishes and “Plat du Mois”—a rotating dish of the month showcasing regional cuisine, meant to share. The wine list boasts more than 100 offerings, with a special focus on Lyon.

restaurants.name: Le Jardinier
restaurants.summary: This chic French restaurant in Midtown has a vegetable-forward menu.
restaurants.description: Le Jardinier is a verdant, sophisticated restaurant at the base of a chic residential tower on the corner of Lexington Avenue and 53rd Street. Helming the kitchen is a Michelin-starred French chef, Alain Verzeroli. Verzeroli is a protégé of the late Joël Robuchon, who was originally slated to be the culinary force here. Look for beautiful vegetable compositions, Dover sole for two and lobster with smoked potatoes. Each meal starts with an “amuse-juice” (perhaps kale, pineapple and ginger), and all house-baked breads are gluten-free.

restaurants.name: Le Pavillon
restaurants.summary: Le Pavillon expresses chef Daniel Boulud’s roots in New York City with a fresh and unique approach to fine dining in a dramatic setting.
restaurants.description: Le Pavillon is a culinary oasis in Midtown East by chef Daniel Boulud. Evoking a “pavillon”, a festive gathering dining space surrounded by nature, Le Pavillon expresses chef Boulud’s roots in New York City with a fresh and unique approach to fine dining in a dramatic setting. With a focus on seasonality and locally sourced ingredients from both land and sea (“terre et mer"), chef Boulud’s celebrated French cuisine, rooted in tradition with a contemporary New York spirit, is at the forefront of the seafood and vegetable-focused menu. Situated in Manhattan’s state-of-the-art-skyscraper One Vanderbilt, Le Pavillon offers a unique setting, both relaxed and inviting with a refined elegance. Designed by Isay Weinfeld, the space boasts a natural landscape composed of lush gardens and tall olive trees living among the tailored dining room and soaring ceilings, evoking a deep sense of natural splendor and genuine serenity.

restaurants.name: Lele's Roman
restaurants.summary: Inspired by the lively neighborhood of Trastevere, Lele’s Roman brings a fresh take on Roman cuisine to Brooklyn's Boerum Hill neighborhood.
restaurants.description: Inspired by the lively neighborhood of Trastevere, Lele’s Roman brings a fresh take on Roman cuisine to Brooklyn's Boerum Hill neighborhood. Led by chef Francesco Battisti, the menu stays true to tradition, from beloved breakfast maritozzi to an all-day selection of Roman classics like amatriciana, cacio e pepe, puntarelle, and carciofi, alongside a selection of shareable pinsas. The beverage program celebrates Italian classics, featuring a robust amaro selection and a thoughtfully curated list of Laziale and regional Italian wines by LDV’s Alessio de Sensi. Designed by Whitley Esteban and Ernesto Gloria of Studio Tre, the space blends the brutalist character of the building with a touch of '70s Italian funk, setting the stage for a love letter to Rome, the city of LDV’s namesake, la dolce vita.

restaurants.name: Leon’s
restaurants.summary: Leon’s is a neighborhood Italian restaurant with French and Egyptian accents from Natalie Johnson and Nick Anderer (also of Anton’s in the West Village).
restaurants.description: Leon’s is a neighborhood Italian restaurant with French and Egyptian accents from Natalie Johnson and Nick Anderer (also of Anton’s in the West Village). The restaurant is inspired by Natalie’s heritage (named after her great grandfather, Leon Hakim) and the couple's travels together across the Mediterranean. Leon’s spotlights Anderer’s deep passion for Italian cuisine, as well as his thoughtful interpretations of treasured Hakim family recipes and culinary traditions passed down by way of Egypt and France. The restaurant’s beverage program, helmed by Johnson, complements and enhances the culinary offerings, highlighting winemakers, brewers, and distillers the couple and their team admire. The restaurant’s lovely, transporting design evokes the quiet, weathered beauty of an Italian seaside town, celebrates natural light, and preserves key architectural details of the building (circa 1895), and the duo spent years hand-selecting the furniture, fixtures, and art that adorn the space.

restaurants.name: Limusina
restaurants.summary: Limusina is a new Mexican restaurant by Quality Branded, inspired by New York City in the 1970s and ‘80s.
restaurants.description: Limusina is a new Mexican restaurant by Quality Branded, inspired by New York City in the 1970s and ‘80s. In that era, nothing was more luxurious than a limousine. The restaurant space was once a taxi and limo depot, a parking garage where drivers would take their cars off-duty to be serviced, grab a bodega coffee and snacks, and loosen their ties before heading back uptown to pick up their clients. The restaurant mirrors that juxtaposition of glam and grit. Limusina has luxe, rich materials and custom fixtures next to raw, exposed concrete columns. Custom light fixtures are affixed to industrial, unfinished ceilings. The restaurant reflects the neighborhood it's in, on the cusp of the shiny, new Hudson Yards and the gritty lower Midtown. Menu favorites include fresh aguachile, queso fundido, long-bone short rib quesabirria, and churritos for dessert.

restaurants.name: Little Alley
restaurants.summary: Chef Yuchun Cheung, born and raised in one of Shanghai’s little alleys in a family of chefs and restaurateurs, decided that Little Alley should recreate the Shanghainese cuisine that he grew up with.
restaurants.description: Little Alley is translated from the Chinese word “弄堂” or “long tang”—the narrow, interconnected alleyways unique to Shanghai—a place where when one family puts a delicious dinner on the table, the aroma of its dishes fills several blocks around. Chef Yuchun Cheung, born and raised in one of Shanghai’s little alleys in a family of chefs and restaurateurs, decided that Little Alley should recreate the Shanghainese cuisine that he grew up with. Leading an entire kitchen staff of Shanghainese locals and drawing experience from his years in the kitchen of Shanghai’s famous Quanjude Restaurant, New York’s China Blue, and most importantly from his childhood home, Chef Cheung designed a menu that’s Shanghainese through and through. In addition, the space offers a nostalgic ambience and interior design resembling that of an old long tang.

restaurants.description: At Maison Passerelle, three-time James Beard Award winner Gregory Gourdet crafts a culinary language all his own, one that links New York and France through the rich flavors of the French Caribbean, French Africa, and French Asia. Located within One Wall Street, the restaurant is a visual feast of custom frescoes, stained glass.. The menu features a prix fixe and tasting menu, all entirely gluten- and dairy-free, celebrating bold, globally inspired flavors with inclusivity at its core. Standouts include Strawberry Grouper with Pepper Confit, Cane Syrup-Glazed Duck with a West African-inspired tamarind jus, and Dry-Aged NY Strip Steak, rubbed in a Haitian coffee, chili, and spice mix. Rounding out the experience are showstopping desserts by executive pastry chef Rachel Green, a compelling wine list, and a rousing lineup of spirited and zero-proof cocktails all by beverage director Ren Neuman.

restaurants.name: Malvan
restaurants.summary: This Carroll Gardens restaurant is named after Malvan, a coastal village in Maharashtra, western India, whose seafood–forward, coconut-rich cuisine has rarely been represented outside its home region.
restaurants.description: Malvan is a coastal village in Maharashtra, western India, whose cuisine has rarely been represented outside its home region. For chef Eric McCarthy, Malvan offered a way to introduce New York to a distinct Indian coastal tradition rooted in everyday village cooking. This is New York’s first restaurant dedicated to Malvani cuisine and McCarthy's second coastal Indian concept, following Indian Table in Cobble Hill, a Goan restaurant shaped by Portuguese influences. A native of Goa, Chef Eric encountered Malvani food while traveling along India’s western coast. Life in Malvan is shaped by the sea and by community. Days begin at the fish markets, kitchens remain open and airy, and meals are cooked slowly and meant to be shared. The cuisine reflects this rhythm, fresh seafood–forward, coconut-rich, and grounded in everyday cooking rather than ceremony or excess.

menu.text:
INSPIRED BY
                       TRADITION
     Malvan is a coastal village in Maharashtra, western India, whose cuisine has rarely been
  represented outside its home region. For Chef Eric McCarthy, Malvan offered a way to introduce
         New York to a distinct Indian coastal tradition rooted in everyday village cooking.

  This is New York’s first restaurant dedicated to Malvani cuisine and Chef Eric’s second coastal
  Indian concept, following Indian Table in Cobble Hill, a Goan restaurant shaped by Portuguese
                                             influences.

A native of Goa, he encountered Malvani food while traveling along India’s western coast and often
describes it as a close cousin to Goan cuisine, connected by ingredients and coastal traditions, yet
                                     defined by its own identity.

 Life in Malvan is shaped by the sea and by community. Days begin at the fish markets, kitchens
 remain open and airy, and meals are cooked slowly and meant to be shared. The cuisine reflects
 this rhythm, fresh seafood–forward, coconut-rich, and grounded in everyday cooking rather than
                                       ceremony or excess.

 At Malvan in Brooklyn, the philosophy is simple. Stay true to the origins. Respect the ingredients.
 Let the flavors speak for themselves. The experience is shaped for a neighborhood setting, warm,
welcoming, and unhurried, while remaining deeply connected to the coastal village that inspired it.

  This is Malvani cooking as it is lived and cooked at home. Honest, soulful, and rooted in place.

restaurants.summary: Markette is a modern European restaurant with Caribbean influences from chef India Doris (previously executive sous chef at two Michelin-starred Saga) and managing partner Alex Pfaffenbach.
restaurants.description: Markette is a modern European restaurant with Caribbean influences from chef India Doris (previously executive sous chef at two Michelin-starred Saga) and managing partner Alex Pfaffenbach (Eleven Madison Park alum and former director of development for Quality Branded—Zou Zou's, Bad Roman and more). The seasonal menu draws inspiration from India's upbringing in London, where British staples were reimagined in a Caribbean household—boldly spiced and full of flavor. It also reflects her culinary journey across Europe, from working in a Normandy brasserie and small local restaurants in Spain to acclaimed London institutions such as La Trompette and Bibendum at the historic Michelin House. The beverage program is helmed by Chris Figueroa (previously of Saga, Crown Shy, and World's 50 Best-recognized Overstory).

Executive chef Braxton Decker presents a refined New American menu that reimagines seasonal ingredients through an elevated, modern lens. Dishes celebrate local flavors while incorporating global technique, delivering plates that are as thoughtful as they are flavorful. The bar program, led by beverage director Kat Foster, offers a meticulously crafted cocktail list highlighting inventive riffs on classic. Please note that the dress code is business casual.

restaurants.name: Meadowsweet
restaurants.summary: At Williamsburg's modern, chic Meadowsweet, executive chef Polo Dobkin has a deft touch with seasonal ingredients, crafting dishes with a Mediterranean bent.
restaurants.description: At Williamsburg's modern, chic Meadowsweet, executive chef Polo Dobkin has a deft touch with seasonal ingredients, crafting dishes with a Mediterranean bent. Crispy artichokes, house-made pastas and octopus with piquillo peppers and chorizo are among the highlights. Rolls hot from the oven are dusted with sea salt, luscious when spread with thyme-honey butter. Dobkin's wife, Stephanie Lempert, has devised some refreshing cocktails that are garnished with fresh herbs harvested from the loft garden overhead. That garden, plus patterned tiled floors, comfortable caramel banquettes and bare wood tables, makes it a pretty place to gather.

restaurants.name: Mermaid Inn - Upper West Side
restaurants.summary: The Mermaid Inn is an American seafood brasserie, replete with style, hospitality and a menu marked by bold and seasonally inspired cuisine.
restaurants.description: The Mermaid Inn - Upper West Side is part of a family of casually sophisticated seafood restaurants born in New York in 2003. Starting out in Manhattan’s East Village as a spot-on rendition of a casual New England fish shack, The Mermaid Inn has morphed into an American seafood brasserie, replete with style, hospitality and a menu marked by bold and seasonally inspired cuisine. The Mermaid Inn has been designed to evoke the feeling of being on a mini-vacation in a small seaside village.

restaurants.name: Metropolis
restaurants.summary: Metropolis is a vibrant contemporary American restaurant from Marcus Samuelsson within the Perelman Performing Arts Center in Lower Manhattan.
restaurants.description: Metropolis by Marcus Samuelsson is a vibrant contemporary American restaurant from Marcus Samuelsson within the Perelman Performing Arts Center. It is the culinary anchor of this new cultural cornerstone of Lower Manhattan. The menu explores the rich culinary traditions of New York City through a modern lens with theatrical cocktails, a fun and worldly wine list, and gracious hospitality. Metropolis, designed by David Rockwell, features a dazzling and yet warmly inviting dining room and a bustling bar, a landscaped outdoor terrace, and a lobby lounge featuring free-to-the-public artistic programming.

restaurants.name: Mezze on the River
restaurants.summary: This casual, family-friendly restaurant on the Manhattan waterfront features shareable dishes such as artichoke and spinach dip and a quartet of mac-n-cheese cones.
restaurants.description: This casual, family-friendly restaurant on the Manhattan waterfront features shareable dishes such as artichoke and spinach dip and a quartet of mac-n-cheese cones. Entrees include sesame-crusted tuna, penne Bolognese and the house burger. Rounding out the menu are salads, desserts and signature cocktail. The indoor décor is classic American bistro, down to the copper-top bar. There’s outdoor seating on two terraces, with views of the Hudson River across to the Colgate Clock.

restaurants.description: Miriam Brooklyn is the original location that opened in Park Slope nearly two decades ago, and remains a neighborhood favorite for all-day brunch and warm, approachable Mediterranean cooking. The menu highlights Israeli-inspired dishes and classic comfort favorites, including burekas, shakshuka, seasonal salads, and shareable plates built for the table. The space feels homey yet lively, working equally well for dates, families, and groups. Hospitality is central to the experience, with an easygoing vibe that keeps locals coming back for both weekday meals and weekend brunch.

restaurants.description: Miriam Upper East Side is an intimate addition to chef Rafael Hasid's Mediterranean-focused portfolio, offering a refined and welcoming dining experience. restaurants.name: Miriam West Village
restaurants.summary: Miriam West Village brings the Brooklyn-born restaurant’s signature hospitality and Israeli-Mediterranean flavors to a lively downtown setting.
restaurants.description: Miriam West Village brings the Brooklyn-born restaurant’s signature hospitality and Israeli-Mediterranean flavors to a lively downtown setting. First launched in Park Slope in 2005, Miriam became known for vibrant brunches and shareable dishes, and this location continues that tradition with a strong dinner scene and a spirited bar program. Guests visit for shakshuka, burekas, and fresh salads during the day, then return at night for mezze, comforting plates, and cocktails in an energetic room with a music-forward vibe. The space feels stylish, welcoming, and built for nights out.

restaurants.name: Miru
restaurants.summary: Perched atop Pier 57 in Chelsea, Miru is a rooftop Japanese listening lounge, rooftop bar and dining destination that offers a tranquil escape by day and a sultry, immersive atmosphere by night.
restaurants.description: Perched atop Pier 57 in Chelsea, Miru is a rooftop Japanese listening lounge, rooftop bar and dining destination that offers a tranquil escape by day and a sultry, immersive atmosphere by night. Curated vinyl soundscapes set the tone amidst uninterrupted views of the Hudson River and the Manhattan skyline, while the food, cocktails and saké transport you. With its seamless flow onto the Pier 57 rooftop park lawn, Miru’s design emphasizes intimacy and discovery. Plush seating, mood lighting and a carefully curated soundscape create the perfect backdrop for a romantic date, a stylish night out, or a late-night gathering with friends. Whether you’re savoring Junmai Daiginjo saké in a private corner booth or dancing under the stars to a live vinyl DJ set, Miru delivers a transportive rooftop dining and nightlife experience—unmistakably New York, with a Tokyo soul.

restaurants.name: Mission Ceviche - Union Square
restaurants.summary: Mission Ceviche, from chef Jose Luis Chavez and partner Brice Mastroluca, has become synonymous with modern Peruvian cuisine, offering a diverse array of dishes crafted from the freshest ingredients.
restaurants.description: Mission Ceviche was born in 2015 when chef Jose Luis Chavez and partner Brice Mastroluca outfitted a modest stall within Gansevoort Market to create an homage to the flavors of Peru. The initial success at Gansevoort Market spurred the establishment of a second fast-casual spot in Canal Street Market, and building on the momentum, the partners took Mission Ceviche to new heights with the opening of its first sit-down restaurant on the Upper East Side in 2019. The restaurant found immediate critical success after launching, earning a star from Pete Wells at the New York Times and a feature in the Michelin Guide. Mission Ceviche has become synonymous with modern Peruvian cuisine, offering a diverse array of dishes crafted from the freshest ingredients.

restaurants.name: Mokyo
restaurants.summary: Mokyo offers an array of Asian-inspired cuisine that blend flavors from chef Kyungmin "Kay" Hyun's childhood and travels across Spain and South America.
restaurants.description: Mokyo is a cozy nook in the East Village. The name is a playful way of saying "Thursday" in Korean ("mok" is the abbreviation "Thurs."), and Mokyo is the sister restaurant to Thursday Kitchen from chef Kyungmin "Kay" Hyun. Mokyo offers an array of Asian-inspired cuisine that blend flavors from Chef Kay’s childhood and travels across Spain and South America. Understanding the inevitable loss to her grandma and mom’s traditional dishes, Chef Kay has found a perfect balance of Asian twists and dishes from her travels to ignite nostalgic flavors yet something unfamiliar and pleasant with an Asian flair.

restaurants.name: Molyvos
restaurants.summary: A meal at this high-end Midtown eatery is sure to put you in a sunny mood.
restaurants.description: Molyvos is a celebration of the Livanos Family’s ancestral hometown on the island of Lesvos, offering a fresh perspective that blends the modern energy and ancient culture that make Greece one of the most spectacular places in the world. Molyvos celebrates the lifestyle and foodways of Greece, bringing filoxenia—Greek style of hospitality—to Hell’s Kitchen, a block from the Theatre District. Molyvos offers a variety of spreads, seasonal raw seafood dishes, whole grilled fish, and beloved classics alongside the country’s largest cellar of wines exclusively from Greece.

restaurants.description: The beloved Japanese restaurant Momoya has added this new incarnation on Manhattan's Upper West Side. Choose from kitchen entrées like teriyaki, Scottish salmon or grass-fed rib eye. Noodle dishes are served with wasabi seaweed tempura and oshinko. The extensive sushi menu features entrées such as the eight-piece sushi, tuna roll or the 15-piece sashimi. Beverages include an international wine list as well as specialty cocktails like the Gin Ray or the Momo splash created with peach sake, rose champagne and orange juice.

The two-level space is surrounded by windows, and has an unencumbered view of the bustle of a busy intersection, and of one of New York’s most historic churches. Inside, however, is a serene scene of Japanese fare that showcases picture-perfect nigiri and sublime foods highlighting the beauty of the vast array of dishes.

restaurants.name: Moono
restaurants.summary: Moono is the second project by chef Hoyoung Kim, building upon the success of his renowned Michelin 1-starred Jua, introducing the vibrant and evolving Korean food culture to New York City.
restaurants.description: Moono is the second project by chef Hoyoung Kim, building upon the success of his renowned Michelin 1-starred Jua. Taking its name from the Korean word for “gateway,” Moono symbolizes a literal “door” to another world and represents a passage to diverse cultures. Housed in a stunning three-story building that is a recognized landmark of New York, Moono's mission is to serve as the ultimate gateway, introducing the vibrant and evolving Korean food culture to New York City, captivating the palates of the new generation.

restaurants.name: Murano Ristorante
restaurants.summary: Executive chef Cesar Dutan infuses elements of Italian, French and Asian flavors into an inspiring menu of authentic Venetian staples and flavors from across Italy with daring twists and visual flair.
restaurants.description: Milan Licul, a legend among New York City restauranteurs, got his start more than 50 years ago, at his family’s small café in Croatia, and by 1983 he launched a restaurant with his friend and fellow countryman Branko Turcinovic, opening the original Murano Ristorante in Manhattan's Garment District, featuring the fine northern Italian dining that became his trademark. This restaurant marks the return of that 1980s-era nameplate. Executive chef Cesar Dutan infuses elements of Italian, French and Asian flavors into his culinary artwork. He has graced the kitchens of many legendary dining rooms, including; Jean George, Amacord, Osteria Stella, Bobby Vans, Felice, Blue Bird London and Delmonico’s Steakhouse. Cesar’s passion for pastas, risottos and Italian classics, paired with his adventurous and positive spirit and approach to cooking, translate into an inspiring menu of authentic Venetian staples and flavors from across Italy with daring twists and visual flair.

restaurants.summary: Musaek is a Korean seafood and cocktail bar rooted in Korean flavors and contemporary technique.
restaurants.description: Located beneath Howoo and DubuHaus, Musaek is a Korean seafood and cocktail bar rooted in Korean flavors and contemporary technique. The name, meaning "colorless" in Korean, reflects the restaurant's philosophy of quiet coexistence, balance, and refinement. Its signature cocktail program focuses on clarified cocktails crafted with Korean ingredients, stripped of color to reveal depth, clarity, and layered character beneath the surface. The food menu draws inspiration from Korea's coastal cuisine, featuring raw, chilled, and warm seafood dishes that capture the ocean's natural brininess, delicate textures, and clean flavors through a modern lens. Reservations are available via Resy, and walk-ins are also welcome.

restaurants.summary: Naks by Unapologetic Foods offers a gastronomic tour of the Philippines framed by the personal memories of the restaurant’s chef, Eric Valdez.
restaurants.description: In Tagalog, the word "Naks" carries the beautiful essence of surprise and admiration, serving as the team's inspiration to craft gastronomic delights that aim to evoke these heartfelt emotions. These meals are meticulously prepared to spark joy and wonder with every flavorful bite. Naks by Unapologetic Foods offers a gastronomic tour of the Philippines framed by the personal memories of the restaurant’s chef, Eric Valdez. Chef Eric is crisscrossing Philippines and taking inspirations from locals homes and smaller towns to present a part of the cuisine that is still hidden from many around the world. There are two ways to experience Naks—a la carte or the communal Kamayan Feast—and each offers its own unique perspective.

restaurants.description: Partners Andy E. Arkun, Erhan Bahceci and Zeynep Tansug brought together a team of Turkish chefs to execute their vision of reimagined regional Turkish cuisine. Nar Restaurant sources produce from the Union Square Farmers Market and proteins from Amish Country in Pennsylvania to serve clean, organic, halal-certified food. restaurants.name: Narkara
restaurants.summary: At Narkara, dining is a cultural journey inspired by the culinary traditions of Northern and Northeastern Thailand.
restaurants.description: At Narkara, dining is a cultural journey inspired by the culinary traditions of Northern and Northeastern Thailand. These regions offer a deeper, lesser-seen expression of Thai cuisine shaped by distinct landscapes and ways of living. In the North, cooler, mountainous terrain gives rise to aromatic, herb-driven dishes, while Northeastern Thai, or Isan cuisine, reflects a hotter, drier climate and a close relationship with the Mekong River, favoring bold, savory and fermented flavors over sweetness or richness. Ingredients such as herbs, chilies, dried spices, sticky rice and preserved elements form the foundation of the cooking. Crafted in-house with care, the menu honors generations of culinary wisdom while embracing thoughtful innovation. Custom bamboo installations, woven pieces, and handcrafted ceramics reflect Thailand’s artistry, allowing Narkara to share the unseen taste of Thailand with New York through food, design and hospitality.

restaurants.description: No Work Allowed (NWA) is a Japanese izakaya with a northeastern Thai twist. It's a unique culinary destination in Midtown East where good food, great drinks, and live music come together in a relaxed, vintage-inspired atmosphere. Founded by a team of food enthusiasts with a passion for American nostalgia and jazz, NWA invites guests to unwind after a long day and experience an unforgettable meal. Leading the kitchen is Hawk Rodman, a talented chef with years of experience in Thai cuisine and training under the renowned chef Masayoshi Takayama at the three Michelin-starred Masa in NYC. Chef Hawk brings a refined fusion of Japanese techniques and Thai flavors to the menu, delivering dishes that are both innovative and comforting. Be sure to try his signature Pad Thai, a tribute to his time with Chef Masa.

restaurants.name: Nonna Dora's - 2nd Avenue
restaurants.summary: Nonna Dora's is an Italian restaurant and pasta bar in Kips Bay serving fresh pasta made daily by Nonna herself.
restaurants.description: Nonna Dora's is an Italian restaurant and pasta bar in Kips Bay serving fresh pasta made daily by Nonna herself. Addolorata Marzovilla, or Nonna Dora, has been making pasta for about 70 years, emigrating to the United States in the 1970s when she was 34. For several years she worked as a seamstress, but when her son, Nicola, opened an Italian restaurant, she offered her pasta making skills and “left the needlework for noodles.” Her expertise in making Puglia-style pasta has earned her the nickname “the pasta machine.”

restaurants.description: Nonna Dora's was created with a simple goal: to allow diners to enjoy the same handmade pasta that the eponymous Dora Marzovilla has been feeding her family for decades. With the original Kips Bay location's popularity quickly outgrowing its size, the newer Tribeca location features a larger dining room and an expanded menu featuring key dishes from the Marzovillas' previous restaurant, I Trulli. Lucky guests can even catch Nonna Dora herself making pasta by hand during lunch hours.

restaurants.summary: Nubiani Midtown East offers a Korean barbecue dining experience where guests gather around the table to enjoy meats grilled over direct heat.
restaurants.description: Nubiani Midtown East offers a Korean barbecue dining experience where guests gather around the table to enjoy meats grilled over direct heat. The name "Nubiani" refers to the traditional Korean style of cooking meat over open fire, a technique that highlights the natural flavor of the ingredients with minimal seasoning. Each table features a built-in grill where guests can cook and share carefully selected cuts of beef and pork alongside classic Korean dishes. Nubiani provides a welcoming setting for business dinners, casual gatherings, and evenings spent enjoying Korean barbecue together.

restaurants.name: Nuyores
restaurants.summary: Nuyores is a bold celebration of South American flavor and New York soul, reimagining Peruvian-inspired cuisine through the City’s vibrant lens.
restaurants.description: Nuyores is a bold celebration of South American flavor and New York soul, reimagining Peruvian-inspired cuisine through the City’s vibrant lens. Led by chef Oscar Lorenzzi (formerly of Contento) and hospitality partner Jonathan Charnay (formerly of Masa), the restaurant brings decades of experience to a lively, shareable dining experience in Manhattan's West Village. Lorenzzi’s cooking is unpretentious yet full of character, rooted in his Peruvian heritage and shaped by New York energy, while Charnay’s refined beverage program offers thoughtful, globally-inspired pairings. The result is a warm, soulful gathering place where South American heritage meets New York style.

restaurants.summary: Devoted and passionate Michelin-recognized chef Maia Acquaviva, the co-founder of Oda House, immerses guests into the flavorful world of traditional Georgian dishes.
restaurants.description: Devoted and passionate Michelin-recognized chef Maia Acquaviva, the co-founder of Oda House, is here to immerse guests into the flavorful world of traditional Georgian dishes. Born and raised in Georgia, Maia has been treasuring hundred-year-old recipes to share in this Georgian cuisine restaurant in New York. Since early childhood, she developed a love for specialties that have been passed down for generations like khachapuri and khinkali. At Oda House, you can always expect to savor the richest and most delectable Georgian cooking delivered by a true Georgian chef.

restaurants.summary: Located on Pier 57 at Hudson River Park in Chelsea, ofCorsica NYC brings the bold flavors and rustic charm of Corsican cuisine to Manhattan.
restaurants.description: Escape to the Mediterranean in New York City. Located on Pier 57 at Hudson River Park in Chelsea, ofCorsica NYC brings the bold flavors and rustic charm of Corsican cuisine to Manhattan. The menu celebrates the sun-drenched coastlines of Corsica with fresh seafood, shareable small plates, and seasonal specialties crafted with authentic Mediterranean tradition. Complementing the menu is the largest Corsican wine collection in New York, paired with a thoughtfully curated selection of Mediterranean-inspired wines and cocktails. Whether you’re heading out for a romantic dinner, a group gathering, or a glass of wine at the bar, ofCorsica offers a one-of-a-kind dining experience with views of the Hudson River.

restaurants.description: Oncheon brings the essence of Korean hot spring culture to New York, creating an oasis from the City's fast pace. Guests are invited to unwind with slow-cooked shabu-shabu and delicately arranged dishes in a serene, restorative setting. Oncheon offers Chanhap rice sets, classic Korean appetizers and various seasonal dishes. Oncheon is Glow Seoul's answer to New York City's long-awaited yearning for truly authentic yet unique Korean cuisine.

restaurants.summary: Find old-school glamour and new-school cocktails at this rooftop bar.
restaurants.description: Set on the 26th-floor rooftop of the historic Beekman Tower, Ophelia takes inspiration from its art deco building, maintaining some of the original 1928 touches while adding velvet booths and a checkerboard floor. The cocktail menu matches the space in its mix of classics (martinis, old-fashioneds) and modern drinks, like Ophelia’s Ascension, which blends mezcal, Sri Lankan palm sugar, bitters and cedar smoke. Even a simple highball feels extra special in the space, whether enjoyed at the 24-foot pewter bar or on the outdoor terrace with 360-degree city views.

restaurants.description: Executive chef Carlos Barroz and his partners in Palermo Argentinian Bistro on Manhattan’s Restaurant Row have opened this second location in Gramercy. restaurants.summary: Meat lovers will love Palermo Argentinian Bistro on Restaurant Row, where beef reigns supreme.
restaurants.description: Meat lovers will love Palermo Argentinian Bistro, where beef reigns supreme. Orhan Cakir, the force behind the Pierre Loti wine bar in Gramercy, has teamed up with executive chef Carlos Barroz, formerly of La Pulperia, to open this latest addition to Manhattan’s Restaurant Row. The steakhhouse draws it inspiration from Palermo, a destination in Buenos Aires known for its fashionable bars and restaurants. Set in a three-story brownstone built in 1894, the bi-level restaurant brings traditional Argentinian barbecue centering on prime steaks sourced from the nearby century-old Piccinini Brothers butcher shop.

restaurants.description: At Palo Santo, you’ll find pan-Latin cooking in a Brooklyn brownstone. Chef Jacques Gautier’s changing menu blends Latin American and Caribbean influences with high-quality, seasonal ingredients including local produce from the nearby Grand Army Plaza Greenmarket. Palo Santo’s wine list has over five dozen wines from South America and New York State. Imported Latin American beers are available in bottles and cans, and local craft brews are on tap.

restaurants.name: Paris Bar
restaurants.summary: Paris Bar is an iconic French brasserie near Carnegie Hall and Central Park that serves traditional French fare from breakfast through supper every day, with brunch available on weekends, plus a rooftop bar.
restaurants.description: Paris Bar is an iconic French brasserie nestled within the Le Meridien hotel near Carnegie Hall and Central Park. They serve traditional French fare from breakfast through supper every day, with brunch available on weekends. Known for its lively ambiance, warm service, and soulful cuisine, the menu features fresh seafood and shellfish as well as signature French dishes such as Beef Bourguignon and bouillabaisse. For those seeking a breathtaking view to accompany their meal, there's Le Jardin Rooftop Bar, offering stunning views of Central Park. It's the perfect spot to unwind with a drink, enjoy a light bite, and take in the cityscape.

restaurants.summary: This seasonal Indian restaurant in the Flatiron District celebrates the intersection of chef Chetan Shetty’s Indian heritage and New York’s culinary vibrancy.
restaurants.description: Passerine is a seasonal Indian restaurant in the Flatiron District led by acclaimed chef Chetan Shetty alongside owners Maneesh K. Goyal and Alvina Patel Buxani. The restaurant celebrates the intersection of Chef Shetty’s Indian heritage and New York’s culinary vibrancy, blending traditional Indian techniques with seasonal ingredients sourced from the Union Square Greenmarket and spice blends crafted by Chef Shetty’s mother in Pune. Guests can savor Chef Shetty’s inventive menu in the intimate Drawing Room, the elegant bar, and the vibrant main dining room. There is also a private dining room located downstairs who can host up to 28 guests. Walk-ins are welcome and reservations are available.

restaurants.description: This casual Italian restaurant offers a full variety of reasonably priced sandwiches, pastas, pizza, chicken, veal and fresh fish dishes. Pasta Lovers also offers private rooms that can accommodate 10 to 80 people; full-service catering for up to 200 is also available, with delivery throughout Manhattan.

restaurants.name: Patrick's on the Hill
restaurants.summary: The menu at this Hamilton Heights restaurant features a mix of traditional Caribbean dishes and creative fusion offerings, with standout favorites like jerk chicken, oxtails, and Jamaican beef patties.
restaurants.description: Patrick's on the Hill, a Caribbean restaurant in Hamilton Heights, West Harlem, in northern Manhattan. The menu features a mix of traditional Caribbean dishes and creative fusion offerings, with standout favorites like jerk chicken, oxtails, and Jamaican beef patties. Wednesday trivia and Sunday live jazz bring the community together. Guests may choose to enjoy their experience at the bar or in the dining room. Walk-ins are always welcome, and reservations are accepted up to 28 days in advance.

restaurants.name: Patsy's Italian Restaurant
restaurants.summary: Serving the Theatre District with their classic Neapolitan menu since 1944, this celebrity hangout has played host to stars like Al Pacino, Robert De Niro, Liza Minnelli and, most famously, Frank Sinatra.
restaurants.description: Serving the Theatre District since 1944 (in their current location since 1954), this celebrity hangout has played host to stars like Al Pacino, Robert De Niro, Liza Minnelli and, most famously, Frank Sinatra. The classic Neapolitan menu features signature dishes such as lobster fra diavolo and veal rollatine marsala, and famed chef Sal Scognamillo, who has been a frequent guest chef on TV (such as the Today show and the Martha Stewart Show), can be spotted on the premises. Reservations are recommended, and the dress code is smart-casual, so shorts are not allowed.

restaurants.name: Pera SoHo
restaurants.summary: Pera SoHo is an eastern Mediterranean retreat inspired by its namesake Istanbul neighborhood.
restaurants.description: Pera SoHo is an eastern Mediterranean retreat inspired by the renowned namesake Istanbul neighborhood where food, culture, nightlife and the cosmopolitan converge. Pera SoHo seduces with an environment that is simultaneously warm and vibrant. The culinary philosophy is to look beyond the current day borders of the eastern Mediterranean and instead appreciate their culinary and cultural richness as a whole. Seasonal garden and rooftop accommodations with 180-degree views of the Manhattan skyline are available.

restaurants.name: Pete's Tavern
restaurants.summary: Pete's Tavern is the oldest continuously operating bar and restaurant in New York City.
restaurants.description: Pete's Tavern, the oldest continuously operating bar and restaurant in New York City, opened its doors in 1864 and remained open as a speakeasy throughout prohibition. Since then, Pete's Tavern has remained exactly as it was when the doors opened, with a beautiful original rosewood bar, pressed tin ceiling and original tiled floor. In 1905, O.Henry wrote "The Gift of the Magi" in the first booth in the bar room. The food, beverages and service are all outstanding, and this historic restaurant is a must-visit for New Yorkers and tourists alike.

restaurants.name: Petite Boucherie
restaurants.summary: Located at the historic intersection of Christopher and Gay Streets, Petite Boucherie brings a touch of France to the cultured and eclectic neighborhood of the West Village.
restaurants.description: Located at the historic intersection of Christopher and Gay Streets, Petite Boucherie brings a touch of France to the cultured and eclectic neighborhood of the West Village. An intimate window-laden, corner restaurant serves French classics like Les Escargots and Steak au Poivre, alongside an extensive wine list. Petite Boucherie is inspired by the elegance of Parisian Belle Époque, and with a hand-crafted menu of timeless​ dishes, the intimate bistro serves as a community hub for engaging conversation.​

restaurants.name: Philippe by Philippe Chow Downtown
restaurants.summary: This newly renovated subterranean dining space offers a family-style menu that emphasizes traditional Beijing cuisine with an elevated twist.
restaurants.description: Philippe by Philippe Chow Downtown continues the brand’s legacy of elegant Chinese dining, bringing chef Philippe Chow’s signature dishes to Chelsea near the Meatpacking District. The subterranean dining space offers a family-style menu that emphasizes traditional Beijing cuisine with an elevated twist, with cult favorites like Chicken Satays, Green Prawns and the legendary Peking Duck. Catering to the buzzy downtown crowd, Philippe by Philippe Chow Downtown features rotating DJs on weekend nights and is open til 2am, serving a special late night menu for those looking for a bite after dark.

restaurants.name: Philippe Chow Fifth Avenue
restaurants.summary: Philippe Chow, the iconic New York fine-dining destination known for more than two decades of tableside Peking Duck and champagne-fueled celebrations, has opened its new flagship at 10 East 52nd Street.
restaurants.description: Philippe Chow, the iconic New York fine-dining destination known for more than two decades of tableside Peking Duck and champagne-fueled celebrations, has opened its new flagship at 10 East 52nd Street. Showcasing modern Beijing-style cuisine with theatrical flair, signature dishes include Whole Peking Duck, Chicken Satay, Sesame Walnut Prawns, Salt & Pepper Lobster and Cotton Candy Baked Alaska. The glamorous, multi-level space offers private dining for up to 300 guests and offsite catering up to 150 miles outside of NYC.

restaurants.name: Pico De Gallo Bar & Kitchen
restaurants.summary: Pico De Gallo Bar & Kitchen blends traditional Mexican cuisine with the personal touch of executive chef Edgar Gomez, who brings more than 20 years of culinary experience.
restaurants.description: At Pico De Gallo Bar & Kitchen, they take pride in blending traditional Mexican cuisine with the personal touch of executive chef Edgar Gomez, who brings more than 20 years of culinary experience. The dishes showcase the highest quality of raw and fresh ingredients. They are committed to providing guests with a first-class dining experience in a relaxing and inviting atmosphere, at an affordable cost. Pico De Gallo Bar & Kitchen offers an immersive atmosphere inspired by Mexican pop art, creating a space where every guest feels welcomed and celebrated.

restaurants.name: Pinky Swear
restaurants.summary: Pinky Swear is an art-forward restaurant and cocktail bar on Manhattan's Lower East Side where creativity, connection, and discovery collide.
restaurants.description: Pinky Swear is an art-forward restaurant and cocktail bar on Manhattan's Lower East Side where creativity, connection, and discovery collide. Interactive installations, rotating exhibitions, creative dishes by chef Will Horowitz, and a vibrant drinks menu are featured in the space where guests are invited to explore, play, and lose themselves in the unexpected—no two nights here are ever the same.

restaurants.name: Prohibition
restaurants.summary: This bar/restaurant offers a wide variety of cocktails, casual American fare and live music every night after 9pm.
restaurants.description: This bar/restaurant, located three blocks from the American Museum of Natural History, offers a wide variety of cocktails, casual American fare and live music every night after 9pm. From Gavin Degraw to Dan Ackroyd to former New York Yankees outfielder Bernie Williams, one never knows just who they might see perform when they come to hang at Prohibition. Menu items include a selection of appetizers—including mini cheeseburgers, macaroni and cheese, fried calamari and buffalo wings—as well as a large dinner menu consisting of comforting American fare.

images.alt: Courtesy, Prohibition

restaurants.name: Psaraki
restaurants.summary: Psaraki, the creation of longtime hospitality veteran James Paloumbis, evokes the charm of seaside tavernas found along the shores of Greece.
restaurants.description: Psaraki, meaning “little fish” in Greek, is the creation of longtime hospitality veteran James Paloumbis. The restaurant evokes the charm of seaside tavernas found along the shores of Greece. It offers spectacular views of the Brooklyn Bridge, the Manhattan skyline, and the Williamsburg Bridge, juxtaposing the tranquility of its serene ambiance with the vibrant energy of nearby Manhattan. Psaraki is a place to unwind, enjoy a perfect cocktail, and savor traditional homemade Greek dishes meant for sharing while escaping NYC's hustle and bustle. Psaraki’s menu is inspired by James’ culinary philosophy, which he terms “homemade,” where each dish is a testament to the authenticity and connection of family recipes, traditionally prepared and presented as if one was a visitor in James’ seaside home. Guests can enjoy a sampling of classic Greek dishes and a selection of Greek island favorites.

restaurants.name: Pulperia Latin Mediterranean Kitchen
restaurants.summary: Pulpería Latin Mediterranean Kitchen serves the flavors of Latin America with Mediterranean touches by executive chef Miguel Molina, who prides himself on his creativity for reimagining dishes.
restaurants.description: As Restaurant Row has long been a culinary destination offering flavors from around the globe, Pulpería Latin Mediterranean Kitchen serves the flavors of Latin America with Mediterranean touches by executive chef Miguel Molina, who prides himself on his creativity for reimagining dishes. At Pulperia, he focuses on fresh, simple, clean, healthy ingredients. The menu offers small plates, paellas, and unique larger fare designed for sharing, plus an extensive cocktail list, all served with the warm hospitality and fun that the Latin culture brings to dining. Leading the team is seasoned restaurateur Orhan Cakir, known for his acclaimed Argentinian steakhouses Palermo Argentinian Steakhouse & Bistro, Palermo Argentinian Bistro Gramercy, and Pierre Loti Wine Bar. Karla Medina, director of operations, brings deep industry knowledge from her experience managing the original La Pulpería location. Now, the beloved concept is reborn as Pulpería Latin Mediterranean Kitchen, refreshed and reimagined for a new era.

restaurants.name: Qanoon
restaurants.summary: Nostalgia and Palestinian comfort food rule at this casual Chelsea spot.
restaurants.description: Qanoon is a nostalgic Middle Eastern tribute to chef-owner Tarek Daka’s vivid memories of his mother’s Palestinian cooking. The contemporary, brick-walled Chelsea space has 40 seats at tables plus 10 at the broad bar. Share thick, satisfying spreads like muhammara, a blend of walnuts, sun-dried peppers and pomegranate molasses (meant to be scooped up with soft pita). The tabbouleh is bright with parsley and mint. Another must-have is a pita pocket sandwich of kofta (meatballs) and cauliflower dripping with tahini.

restaurants.name: Raf's
restaurants.summary: The hearth-driven menu threads the needle through the south of France and Italy, highlighting dishes such as cast iron sfincione (Sicilian pizza), wood-kissed escargot, and dry-aged côte de bôeuf.
restaurants.description: From the team behind the Michelin-starred downtown favorite, The Musket Room, comes Raf’s—a European-style neighborhood dining room and bakery located in Manhattan's NoHo neighborhood. The century-old space is layered in history, with wood-fired ovens dating back to the 1930s. The hearth-driven menu threads the needle through the south of France and Italy, highlighting dishes such as cast iron sfincione (Sicilian pizza), wood-kissed escargot, and dry-aged côte de bôeuf. With a focus on Island and Coastal wines and masterfully crafted classic cocktails, bar seats are available nightly for walk-in guests. Or stop by in the morning for fresh pastries, breads and espresso.

restaurants.name: Restaurant Nippon
restaurants.summary: Opened in 1963, Restaurant Nippon became the first Japanese restaurant in the United States with an authentic sushi bar.
restaurants.description: Nippon has been the heartbeat of authentic Japanese cuisine in New York City since 1963. It's an East Midtown restaurant where tradition meets innovation in a setting as timeless as their heritage. The team at Nippon invites guests to indulge in a culinary journey through traditional Edo-mae (Tokyo) style dishes. Experience their signature dish, the iconic beef negimayaki, a dish that originated at Nippon and has since become a global favorite. Delight in the tempura straight from the tempura bar, a standout feature of their menu. Nippon also takes pride in their in-house creations, including premium ni-hachi soba noodles and house-made tofu, which elevate every dish to an extraordinary level. For a truly authentic experience, reserve the Japanese-style tatami room, a private space designed for intimate gatherings with traditional floor seating and elegant décor.

restaurants.name: Rialto Ristorante
restaurants.summary: Rialto Ristorante is the culmination of restaurateur Milan Licul's storied history in the Italian fine dining space with a nod to modern presentation and palates.
restaurants.description: Restaurateur Milan Licul is a legend among New York City restaurateurs. He got his start in the business more than 50 years ago, at his family’s small café in Croatia, and by 1983 he launched Arno Ristorante with his friend and fellow countryman Branko Turcinovic, operating 40 years strong, and opened the original Murano Ristorante on 36th Street in the Garment District, featuring the fine northern Italian dining that became his trademark. He now operates Arno Ristorante, Murano Ristorante, Alexander's Prime in Ormond Beach, Bukaleta Ristorante and many more in the pipeline. Rialto Ristorante is the culmination of Licul's storied history in the Italian fine dining space with a nod to modern presentation and palates.

restaurants.name: Ribalta
restaurants.summary: This Greenwich Village pizzeria specializes in traditional Neapolitan pies and composed Italian dishes.
restaurants.description: Set in Greenwich Village, Ribalta is "where the heart of Naples meets the energy of New York." The menu brings together classic Neapolitan pizza, fresh pasta and well-loved Italian appetizers made with skill and tradition. Each dish is prepared with care, using quality ingredients that honor real Italian cooking. Whether sharing plates or choosing a favorite, guests will find straightforward, honest food that feels both familiar and special. Every visit offers a warm atmosphere, skilled craftsmanship and a place to enjoy food rooted in tradition and community.

restaurants.name: Rynn Thai Restaurant & Bar
restaurants.summary: Whether you are a Thai food enthusiast or someone new to the cuisine, Rynn Thai Restaurant & Bar offers the vibrant tapestry of Thai cuisine.
restaurants.description: Rynn Thai Restaurant & Bar was founded in the East Village by a group of women who have the same dreams and goals. "Rynn" (รินน์) means to pour—the owners pour their memories into their dishes and glasses—and the restaurant is a place where memories come to life through the art of culinary creations and mixology. Every dish and cocktail they serve is carefully crafted using ingredients and details inspired by the memories and childhood experiences of the owners. It's a place where nostalgia blends with creativity to create a unique and unforgettable dining experience. Whether you are a Thai food enthusiast or someone new to the cuisine, Rynn offers the vibrant tapestry of Thai cuisine. The restaurant has 30 seats in the dining area plus 8 bar seats and 6 more seats for outdoor dining.

restaurants.name: Sadie's
restaurants.summary: Sadie's serves New American comfort classics in their two-level, full-service dining room in the historic Seaport, and the Garden Bar is their open-air social hub.
restaurants.description: Sadie's serves New American comfort classics in their two-level, full-service dining room in the historic Seaport. The kitchen takes an unfussy approach to comfort food—the kind of menu that works equally well for a leisurely weekend brunch or a proper sit-down dinner. Expect familiar favorites executed with real intention: smashed burgers, beer-battered fish and chips, hush puppies with maple butter, and desserts that feel like classics worth revisiting. Sadie's Garden Bar is their open-air social hub. Built for spontaneity, all seating is on a first-come, first-served basis. Just show up, find your spot, and let an afternoon become an evening. The drinks are refreshing and endlessly repeatable: sun-soaked spritzes, crowd-pleasing cocktails, and zero-proof options designed for unhurried rounds with friends. Keep an eye out for gameday watch parties, live music, and marquee cultural events happening on the cobblestones.
