restaurants.name: Salt + Charcoal
restaurants.summary: Salt + Charcoal is Williamsburg’s one of a kind Japanese robata grill and bar.
restaurants.description: Salt + Charcoal is Williamsburg’s one of a kind Japanese robata grill and bar. Preparation of their signature steaks start with the chef hand selecting each piece of beef at the purveyor. It is then dry-aged for 28 to 50 days before charcoal-grilling using their unique crank grill. The result is a super-tender steak with all of the umami trapped inside. Salt + Charcoal also has a wide selection of seafood, a raw bar, and Japanese-inspired appetizers. The full bar features original cocktails crafted by award-winning mixologists, a variety of Japanese spirits, and wines specially crafted to pair with the food offerings.

restaurants.summary: San Carlo Osteria Piemonte is a corner of Turin in Soho.
restaurants.description: San Carlo Osteria Piemonte is like a corner of Turin in Soho. The restaurant, with its minimalist and elegant design, serves dishes that are well-crafted, beautifully presented Piedmont specialties that are reproduced with passion and flair. Evenings can start with a vermouth-based cocktail, just like in an old Torinese cafe, and continue with a Fassona chopped beef, then tajarin pasta with truffle or homemade agnolotti pockets with roast sauce. The kitchen is from Piedmont and so wine is abundant, and not just Nebbiolotry—try the peppery rhythm of a good Pelaverga.

restaurants.name: Scarpetta
restaurants.summary: It all started in a Greek revival townhouse on the edge of the Meatpacking District, where LDV Hospitality brought an unexpected and soulful touch to Italian cuisine.
restaurants.description: It all started in a Greek revival townhouse on the edge of the Meatpacking District, where LDV Hospitality brought an unexpected and soulful touch to Italian cuisine. Scarpetta now resides in the NoMad neighborhood. An Italian expression that means ‘little shoe,’ or the shape bread takes when used to soak up a dish, Scarpetta represents the pure pleasure of savoring a meal down to its very last bite.

address.raw: The James New York—NoMad, 88 Madison Ave.,Manhattan,10016,NY

restaurants.name: Seahorse
restaurants.summary: This modern seafood restaurant and raw bar in Union Square offers an elevated take on coastal dining with pristine seafood, vibrant crudo and seasonal produce sourced from the nearby Greenmarket.
restaurants.description: Seahorse is a modern seafood restaurant and raw bar in Union Square from New York restaurateur John McDonald (Lure Fishbar, Bowery Meat Company). Led by executive chef John Villa, the restaurant offers an elevated take on coastal dining with pristine seafood, vibrant crudo and seasonal produce sourced from the nearby Greenmarket. Designed by Rockwell Group, Seahorse is located inside the landmark Guardian Life building at W New York - Union Square.

restaurants.name: Sei Less
restaurants.summary: Curiously nestled behind an enigmatic mural in Midtown, behind a blink-and-you’ll-miss-it door stands Sei Less, an Asian fusion restaurant with an exclusive flair.
restaurants.description: Curiously nestled behind an enigmatic mural in Midtown, behind a blink-and-you’ll-miss-it door stands Sei Less, an Asian fusion restaurant with an exclusive flair. Set near the Garment District and Madison Square Garden, it's the spot to stop at before or after an event. Sei Less is a hotspot for a romantic date night in a dark corner or a place for a larger party. From album release parties to business meetings, to private events, Sei Less does it all with an air of elegant exclusivity. Dress code is Casual Elegant and entry is subject to doorman discretion.

restaurants.name: Sempre Oggi
restaurants.summary: Born from Italian tradition and heritage, executive Chef Phillip Basone's menu takes seasonal and local ingredients and places them center stage.
restaurants.description: Directly translated as "Always Today," Sempre Oggi focuses on embracing the very best of right now. Born from Italian tradition and heritage, executive Chef Phillip Basone's menu takes seasonal and local ingredients and places them center stage. Brought forth by Robert Guarino in partnership with Simon Oren of Chef Driven Hospitality, Sempre Oggi draws inspiration from renowned Italian architect and designer, Gio Ponti. The bar's handmade ceramic tiles mimic Ponti's worldwide collaboration with Ceramica D'Agostino. A custom floating chandelier nods to Ponti's love for playing with geometric forms, light and color; at once both modern and traditional.

restaurants.name: Sereneco
restaurants.summary: Sereneco is an all-day restaurant in Greenpoint that serves seasonal New American cuisine alongside creative drinks.
restaurants.description: Sereneco is an all-day restaurant that serves seasonal New American cuisine for dinner and brunch, alongside creative drinks, in Greenpoint. Menu highlights include braised beef short rib (creamy polenta, grilled corn, cucumber, pickled red onions, port wine reduction sauce) and Hudson Valley duck confit (braised borlotti beans, grilled cipollini onions, cherry tomatoes, crispy brussels sprouts, sage). The cocktails include the Fly Fig Fly (bourbon, fig, lemon, rosemary) and the Supernova (dill aquavit, gin, cucumber juice, jalapeno, lemon).

The beverage selection is equally impressive, featuring craft cocktails, selected wines, beer, and spirits.

restaurants.name: Shogun Omakase
restaurants.summary: Shogun Omakase is a purveyor of fine Japanese dining where every dish is carefully prepared by their chefs with care and quality in mind.
restaurants.description: Located in the Murray Hill neighborhood of East Midtown, Manhattan, Shogun Omakase is a purveyor of fine Japanese dining. The folks at Shogun are proud of their culture and traditions, and strive to create an atmosphere that conveys the essence of Japan and provides a true taste of its unique flavors. Every dish is carefully prepared by their chefs with care and quality in mind. They use only the freshest seasonal ingredients so that guests can savor each flavor as it was meant to be tasted. The meals are designed to provide an unforgettable experience for every guest. Start off with one of their renowned sushi dishes—each prepared with precision by their master chef. Then enjoy succulent tempura vegetables cooked in light oil for maximum flavor and texture. Or try one of tje grilled dishes cooked over a charcoal fire for that extra smoky flavor.

restaurants.name: Sicily Osteria
restaurants.summary: Located on Restaurant Row in Manhattan's Theatre District, Sicily Osteria is a dining destination that appeals to local residents and office workers, as well as Broadway theatergoers.
restaurants.description: Located on Restaurant Row in Manhattan's Theatre District, Sicily Osteria is a dining destination that appeals to local residents and office workers, as well as Broadway theatergoers. The restaurant offers several dining experiences, from its more formal main dining room that exudes a rustic elegance enhanced by vintage green walls, exposed brick, custom tiled floor and white tablecloths. It's front dining room features an expansive bar, perfect for casual dining; plus, several bistro-style tables; and in the far back, a spacious, naturally lit, enclosed patio garden and atrium transports guests to a lush garden oasis.

restaurants.name: Siren Oyster Bar & Restaurant
restaurants.summary: Siren is a contemporary European seafood restaurant in South Slope, Brooklyn, specializing in modern dishes and an extensive oyster selection.
restaurants.description: It’s fitting that Siren Oyster Bar & Restaurant is named after the deep-sea temptresses, as it is very difficult to escape the call of their snow crab legs, caviar, crab cakes, and lobster bisque. Siren is a contemporary European seafood restaurant in the South Slope area between Park Slope and Greenwood Heights, specializing in modern dishes and an extensive oyster selection. Their hibiscus margarita is a cocktail highlight. The folks at Siren pride themselves on being a local Brooklyn restaurant where friends and family make memories while enjoying the perfect bite or the best cocktails.

restaurants.name: Sistina
restaurants.summary: Sistina has impressed its clientele for more than 40 years with inspired cuisine that is matched by an outstanding wine list, impeccable service and attractive decor.
restaurants.description: Sistina, one of the highest-rated Italian restaurants in New York City, has impressed its clientele for more than 40 years. The restaurant’s inspired cuisine is matched by an outstanding wine list, impeccable service and attractive decor. As soon as guests enter, they are witness to Sistina's romantic ambience, candles and fresh flower arrangements. Cast-iron wall hangings show the whimsical side of the fratelli Bruno. But patrons keep returning for the brothers’ abilities to make simple dishes taste like creative masterpieces.

restaurants.name: Skinos
restaurants.summary: Skinos is a destination where culture and hospitality come alive. The menu brings Greek flavor into the now: fresh, vibrant, and full of character.
restaurants.description: Skinos was created to bring the warmth and energy of Mykonos to New York City. Every detail, from the vibrant ambiance to the sleek design, reflects Mediterranean life at its best. It is a full-sensory escape—the hum of conversation, the rhythm of a live DJ, cocktails glowing under candlelight, plates made to share. It's where dinner flows into nightlife, and every table feels like the best seat in the house. More than a restaurant, Skinos is a destination where culture and hospitality come alive. The menu brings Greek flavor into the now: fresh, vibrant, and full of character. Every dish blends top-quality ingredients with creative flair, from shareable mezze to signature mains designed for lively, effortless dining.

restaurants.description: The good ol’ boys from Dallas who are in New York on business love this upscale steak joint with portions big enough to fill up even a Texas-size appetite. restaurants.name: So & So's
restaurants.summary: This sumptuously-appointed, dimly-lit piano-bar-meets-supper-club evokes the feeling of stumbling into a local legend’s living room during a night out in NYC—but is also an ode to Broadway.
restaurants.description: This sumptuously-appointed, dimly-lit piano-bar-meets-supper-club evokes the feeling of stumbling into a local legend’s living room during a night out in NYC—but is also an ode to Broadway and the theatrical pedigree of Hell’s Kitchen. So & So’s space is anchored by an upright blue piano on a raised stage—an homage to practice rooms and rehearsal studios. Luxurious red banquettes, upholstered walls and custom lighting take cues from vintage City nightlife, and the entertainment features everyone from local acts to Broadway stars and A-list talent, with special guest pop-ups possible.

restaurants.name: Socarrat Paella Bar - Chelsea
restaurants.summary: Socarrat Paella Bar Chelsea reflects an ambiance rich in warmth, comfort and hospitality, and brings out the Spaniard in New York: it's elegant, bold and sexy. A neighborhood staple comprised primarily of one large communal table with a bar and smaller communal tables scattered throughout, Socarrat Chelsea also has a private dining room that can can accommodate up to 28 people.
restaurants.description: Socarrat Paella Bar Chelsea reflects an ambiance rich in warmth, comfort and hospitality, and brings out the Spaniard in New York: it's elegant, bold and sexy. A neighborhood staple, the restaurant is a destination for those looking to experience a little bit of Spain in Chelsea. There are wines from all Spanish regions and a number of specials, including happy hour.

restaurants.name: Society Cafe
restaurants.summary: Hidden inside Walker Hotel is Society Cafe, a market-to-table American restaurant by chef Nicholas McCann.
restaurants.description: With more 20 years of experience in the kitchen, Nicholas McCann, now executive chef of Society Cafe, has always been passionate about food. Drawing inspiration from his family recipes, Nicholas quickly fell in love with the culinary world at a young age and began his career at The French Culinary Institute in NYC. Since then, he has worked with some of the City’s most acclaimed chefs and restaurants, including working alongside chef Luis Bollo of Salinas before moving on to become an executive chef at Tessa, The Milling Room, and Corkbuzz. At Society Cafe, chef Nicholas flexes his creativity by bringing a fresh perspective to the restaurant’s ‘market-to-table’ concept. With a rotating seasonal menu reflective of the City’s local farmers and markets, guests can expect to experience chef Nicholas’ unique culinary creations alongside its intimate and classic art deco inspired space.

restaurants.name: Sofrito on the Hudson
restaurants.summary: Throw back a mojito in the dimly lit bar and savor authentic and affordable Latin American cuisine.
restaurants.description: After throwing back a mojito in the dimly lit bar—where rows of liquor bottles are sleekly backlit in blue—and savoring authentic and affordable Puerto Rican cuisine, you’ll quickly get the feeling that you’re not on Sutton Place anymore. Start your meal at Sofrito with an assortment of empanadas or a Puerto Rican-style gumbo, followed by a plate of arroz con pollo (chicken and rice), ropa vieja (shredded beef) or a heaping paella. Sofrito features live Latin music six days a week, with DJs spinning on Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights.

restaurants.name: Steak Frites Bistro
restaurants.summary: Chef/owner Adam Schop brings classic French fare, in an environment familiar to popular bistros found on the side streets of Paris, to Hell’s Kitchen.
restaurants.description: At his Steak Frites Bistro, chef/owner Adam Schop brings classic French fare, in an environment familiar to popular bistros found on the side streets of Paris, to Hell’s Kitchen. His French cuisine is presented through a New York lens, marrying the two cultures and adding another level of familiarity. Steak Frites Bistro’s dinner menu is concise and provides options for every diner—from those looking to indulge in a multicourse French meal to those on the hunt for a quick, delicious bite—including French, Francophiles, and neighborhood clientele.

restaurants.name: STK Midtown
restaurants.summary: Simply put, STK is not your daddy's steakhouse.
restaurants.description: Simply put, STK is not your daddy's steakhouse. The restaurant brings high-energy dining to Manhattan, breaking down the barriers of a normal steakhouse by losing the overly masculine vibe that has long been the trademark of the genre. Maintaining the quality of a traditional steakhouse and simultaneously reinventing the ambiance, clientele and atmosphere, STK introduces the sensibility of a flirty and feminine steakhouse to a young, sexy market. STK offers a bustling bar that builds on the energy of a DJ spinning tracks nightly. The restaurant layout and striking décor create an intimate, one-of-a-kind dining experience.

restaurants.name: Strip House Downtown
restaurants.summary: Strip House Downtown delivers on dishes and décor, creating a steakhouse unlike any other in New York.
restaurants.description: Strip House Downtown delivers on dishes and décor, creating a steakhouse unlike any other in New York. The menu by executive chef John Schenk features prime cuts of beef charred to perfection, signature side dishes such as truffle creamed spinach and goose fat potatoes, and the famed 24-layer chocolate cake. The wine list is comprehensive and interesting. Part of the experience is the sumptuous, all-red decor, mood lighting and vintage black-and-white photographs. These rare images of captivating females from the original 1900s Studio Manasse collection reference an era of decadence and seduction. Reservations are suggested.

restaurants.name: Sweet Catch
restaurants.summary: Sweet Catch is an ode to the connection between African-American people and their rich history of seafood culinary mastery.
restaurants.description: From the low country of Charleston, South Carolina to the clear blue waters of the Chesapeake Bay, down through the muddy swamps and rushing rivers of the Louisiana Bayou, African-Americans boast a rich history of seafood culinary mastery, a connection to the land, and a respect for the fruits of the sea. Sweet Catch is an ode to this connection—a love letter to African-American culture, African-American people, and African-American love; a place of remembrance for what history has erased and a celebration of their spirit.

restaurants.name: Tachi
restaurants.summary: At Tachi's intimate 12-seat sushi counter, chef Victor Chen crafts a modern Edomae-style omakase featuring market-driven fish, warm seasoned rice, and a progression of bite-sized courses.
restaurants.description: Tachi brings the spirit of Tokyo’s standing sushi counters to Hell's Kitchen in Midtown Manhattan, steps from Times Square’s theaters and landmarks. At its intimate 12-seat bar, chef Victor Chen crafts a modern Edomae-style omakase featuring market-driven fish, warm seasoned rice, and a progression of bite-sized courses designed for a fast-paced yet exceptional dining experience. With roots in celebrated kitchens including Kintsugi and Aman Nama, Chef Chen combines technical precision with a warm, approachable style. Sleek, minimal interiors and thoughtful service make Tachi a destination for both sushi connoisseurs and curious first-timers.

restaurants.name: Takumen
restaurants.summary: Restorative bowls of ramen, sashimi and sushi rolls are served up at this hip izakaya.
restaurants.description: The casual izakaya Takumen feels like a cozy Japanese cottage, with pitched wooden slats over the tables and cheeky prints on the walls. The kitchen is open, and a compact bar displays shelves of highly sought-after sake. In addition to sashimi, sushi rolls and restorative ramen noodles are big salads like black sesame and kale with fried peanuts. Hawaiian tuna poke is another standout, the rosy fish cubes heaped over rice and circled by avocado salad, seaweed salad, potato salad, tangy cauliflower and broccoli.

restaurants.summary: Talavera brings authentic Mexican cuisine to Hell's Kitchen, centered on quality ingredients and traditional techniques, with dishes created for sharing and a contemporary approach to classic Mexican cooking.
restaurants.description: Talavera brings authentic Mexican cuisine to Hell's Kitchen, just steps from Hudson Yards. The menu centers on quality ingredients and traditional techniques, with dishes created for sharing and a contemporary approach to classic Mexican cooking. The space combines a full dining room, bar, outdoor seating and private rooms, making it a flexible choice for lunch, dinner, and weekend brunch. The experience pairs familiar Mexican influences with updated presentations, alongside a cocktail program focused on margaritas and bar favorites. Whether guests are meeting friends or planning a casual evening, Talavera is a Mexican restaurant offering a comfortable setting for everyday meals and group gatherings.

restaurants.name: Tara Kitchen TriBeCa
restaurants.summary: Chef Aneesa Waheed brings the flavors of North Africa to the US.
restaurants.description: The dishes at Tara Kitchen come from founder and executive chef Aneesa Waheed, who fell in love with the country (and her future husband) when visiting Morocco years ago. She then returned home and opened her restaurant in 2012 to help bring the flavors of North Africa to the U.S. On the menu are sharing plates like a spicy chickpea bowl, marinated olives and zaalouk (eggplant blended with tomatoes and garlic), plus salads and dips. Moroccan entrees like grilled lamb kebab and mixed vegetable couscous sit alongside a selection of chicken, lamb and vegetable tagines. Waheed has also taken comfort foods like cabbage rolls, fish cakes and shepherd’s pie and given them a Moroccan twist. The restaurant is also accommodating to vegans and those with food allergies.

This NoMad location also has four incredible loft spaces for private events, and offers full-service catering on and off site.

restaurants.description: Tasca (Iberian for "tavern") brings together the vibrant flavors and culinary traditions of both Spain and the islands of the Latin Caribbean: Puerto Rico, the Dominican Republic and Cuba. restaurants.name: Tavern on the Green
restaurants.summary: One of NYC's most recognizable restaurants is tucked just inside Central Park. It serves up American fare in an elegant indoor-outdoor setting.
restaurants.description: Restaurateurs Jim Caiola and David Salama have created a Tavern on the Green for this generation of diners. Jim and David's aim to re-establish Tavern on the Green as a restaurant for all, New Yorkers and visitors alike, restores this renowned dining hub to its Upper West Side neighborhood. Tavern on the Green celebrates New York and Central Park in all its glory, embracing the limitless, delicious foods for which this diverse culinary city is known. The menu by Executive Chef Tomas Surowka is celebratory and accessible with a nod to Tavern's storied history.

restaurants.name: The Dolar Shop Hot Pot
restaurants.summary: The Dolar Shop's philosophy is to continuously innovate, always serve fresh ingredients, and to excel in customer service to build a strong connection with their guests, and proudly showcase the Macau hot pot culture.
restaurants.description: The Dolar Shop Hot Pot story began in the Las Vegas of the East: Macau. The name “Dolar” comes from a Chinese term embodying the people’s willingness to work hard to gather prosperity, fortune, and never turning down any opportunities. And "Shop?"... they are artisans in their workshop, and their craft is hot pot. Be prepared to indulge in the delectable house-made ingredients. Hot Pot is one of the most beloved ways of dining in Chinese culture. Influences from both the East and West in Macau led to love for home-made fish balls and slices of high-grade beef. These top notch ingredients paired with the blend of sauces makes it a unique experience. The Dolar Shop's philosophy is to continuously innovate, always serve fresh ingredients, and to excel in customer service to build a strong connection with their guests, and proudly showcase the Macau hot pot culture.

restaurants.description: The Dram Shop Bar is a locally owned sports bar and restaurant in Park Slope, Brooklyn. For over 15 years, Dram Shop has been serving classic American dishes with a Tex-Mex twist—chicken wings, the Dram burger, salads, nachos, tacos, and more—all made fresh daily, alongside a wide selection of beers, liquors and cocktails, served by a friendly and welcoming staff. Dram Shop is the perfect destination to eat and drink, watch your favorite team, play pool and have fun. They offer indoor and outdoor dining, games, vegetarian options, free delivery, and they're family friendly.

restaurants.description: Breathtaking views of the Brooklyn Bridge and Jean-Georges Vongerichten’s seafood-centric menu are reason enough to head to the end of Pier 17 in the Seaport. restaurants.name: The Ivory Peacock
restaurants.summary: The Ivory Peacock offers distinct, imaginative cocktails complemented by a variety of vibrant shareable plates.
restaurants.description: Perched within Manhattan's Flatiron and NoMad neighborhoods, The Ivory Peacock pays homage to its original location, which boasts 139 years of history as a bona fide neighborhood destination. As such, they pride themselves on offering distinct, imaginative cocktails complemented by a variety of vibrant shareable plates. The cocktail program, led by head bartenders Carlos Soto and Daniel Benitez, is filled with seasonal spins on classic cocktails utilizing technical French kitchen techniques. The culinary roster includes a raw bar with fresh oysters arriving daily and a selection of familiar French fare—deemed "luxe finger food" by chef Grayson Altenberg.

restaurants.name: The Kunjip
restaurants.summary: This beloved Koreatown eatery serves up authentic entrees, casseroles and barbecue.
restaurants.description: Traditionally, the "Kunjip" (or "big house" in English) is where Koreans visit for family celebrations and special feasts. The Kunjip, one of the oldest Korean BBQ restaurants in Manhattan's Koreatown, offers that same celebratory experience every time guests enter. This beloved eatery serves up authentic entrees, casseroles and barbecue. The folks at this family-run business put their hearts and souls into offering diners an authentic, delicious Korean BBQ experience. The menu features something for everyone, with a diverse mix of flavors and traditional Korean favorites. They believe that using the freshest ingredients—many of which are grown on their own family farm—is what turns any meal at The Kunjip into a special celebration. The Kunjip offers an extensive selection of beer, soju, and traditional Korean wine and sake to accompany your meal.

The menu features a variety of creative dishes, from standard American fare to delicious and hearty traditional Irish fare with a New York twist. Like any good (spirits) library, they stock a large selection of Irish whiskeys, single malts, top-shelf liquors, craft cocktails and fine wines. In addition to domestic and imported draught beers, rotating craft beers, they also offer beers by the bottle/can.

restaurants.name: The Noortwyck
restaurants.summary: Set in the West Village, The Noortwyck exudes an elegant yet intimate charm, offering a timeless, New American menu that celebrates seasonal dishes, an extensive wine selection and specialty cocktails.
restaurants.description: Set in the West Village, The Noortwyck exudes an elegant yet intimate charm, offering a timeless, New American menu that celebrates seasonal dishes, an extensive wine selection and specialty cocktails. Founded by executive chef Andy Quinn and sommelier Cedric Nicaise, the restaurant is committed to delivering the best quality for each guest and supporting the local community. Embracing the ethos of sourcing from nearby New York purveyors, The Noortwyck crafts everything in-house, from pasta and breads to dry aging. The wine list reflects both the team’s interest and Cedric’s expertise, curated to cater to the diverse tastes of their guests, running the full gamut of styles, from earthy and funky to clean and fruity. Garnering acclaim from critics and locals alike, The Noortwyck is “the middle ground between grandeur and informality.”

restaurants.summary: At The Parliament, located in the landmark Benjamin Royal Sonesta New York hotel, chef Rakmin Lee brings to life his vision of a contemporary American Bistro dining menu.
restaurants.description: The Parliament serves breakfast, lunch, dinner and weekend brunch, seven days a week. The restaurant is conveniently located in Manhattan's Midtown East, within walking distance to Rockefeller Center, Broadway, the United Nations and Grand Central Terminal. At The Parliament, chef Rakmin Lee brings to life his vision of a contemporary American Bistro dining menu. The menu offers signature American cuisine, concentrating on seasonal ingredients prepared with classic techniques. The Parliament is located at The Benjamin Royal Sonesta, a restored 1927 Emery Roth hotel, a New York City Landmark and a fitting complement to the restaurant’s refined style, café culture, and eclectic interior design.

restaurants.name: The Wolfe
restaurants.summary: The Wolfe is a sports bar and restaurant inspired by Tom Wolfe, the late novelist and long-time NYC resident.
restaurants.description: The Wolfe is a sports bar and restaurant inspired by Tom Wolfe, the late novelist and long-time NYC resident, whose more well-known works include The Electric Kool-Aid Acid Test, The Right Stuff, and The Bonfire of the Vanities. The Wolfe aims to provide a classy place to enjoy food, sports and events. The decor and menu include nods to Wolfe, such as a cocktail called The Bonfire, a twist on an old fashioned with mezcal, reposado and smoked agave liquor. The menu runs from dry-rubbed chicken wings to mango Thai noodle to "Everything Crusted" ahi tuna.

restaurants.name: Tinos
restaurants.summary: Named after the picturesque Greek island known for its rich culture and stunning views, Tinos combines the charm of the Mediterranean with the taste of time-honored recipes.
restaurants.description: Tinos is a warm and welcoming traditional Greek restaurant that brings the authentic flavors of Greece right to your table. Named after the picturesque Greek island known for its rich culture and stunning views, Tinos combines the charm of the Mediterranean with the taste of time-honored recipes. Their menu is crafted with love and features fresh and high-quality ingredients. Step into Tinos and be transported to the sun-soaked shores of the Aegean, with rustic decor that echoes the blue-and-white palette of Greek architecture, complemented by warm wooden accents and cozy lighting. Whether you’re there to enjoy a hearty family feast or share a romantic dinner for two, the attentive staff ensures that every moment is infused with the spirit of Greek hospitality, known as "philoxenia."

restaurants.name: Togyushi
restaurants.summary: Togyushi blends two experiences: a fine dining omakase counter showcasing traditional techniques, and a more casual wagyu bistro bar and lounge offering small plates, signature cocktails and Japanese vinyl culture.
restaurants.description: Togyushi is a progressive Japanese dining destination centered on the art of wagyu tasting. Bringing the rare GI Zao Wagyu from Yamagata, sourced exclusively from female cattle, to Midtown Manhattan, Togyushi invites guests to explore wagyu in its purest form. The restaurant blends two experiences: a fine dining omakase counter showcasing traditional techniques like warayaki straw-searing and rice-bran fermentation, and a more casual wagyu bistro bar and lounge offering small plates, signature cocktails and Japanese vinyl culture.

restaurants.name: Trapizzino
restaurants.summary: Sink your teeth into Italian-style stuffed sandwich pockets on the Lower East Side.
restaurants.description: Trapizzino looks like a spiffy Lower East Side slice joint, but its Italian street food is of a slightly different nature: overstuffed triangles of pizza bianca. Stefano Callegari, a Roman chef and entrepreneur, coined the term, combining tramezzino (triangular sandwich) and pizza. The pockets have a crisp exterior and soft interior that absorbs the juices from hearty oxtail ragu and eggplant parmigiana. Eight fillings rotate daily. While the trapizzini are designed to be portable, they’re big and messy—so it’s wise to enjoy them at a copper-topped table along with some Italian wine or beer.

restaurants.name: Trattoria Dell'Arte
restaurants.summary: A favorite of concert goers at nearby Carnegie Hall, Trattoria Dell'Arte is a design landmark, thanks to an interior done by the legendary Milton Glaser, and a entrance marked by a giant white nose.
restaurants.description: A favorite of concertgoers at nearby Carnegie Hall, Trattoria Dell'Arte is a design landmark, thanks to an interior done by the legendary Milton Glaser, and a entrance marked by a giant white nose. The kitchen serves homey Italian fare, done to high standards: pizza with a nicely singed crust; osso bucco, served with tomatoes, tart capers and risotto; and a seafood pappardelle, with a white-wine sauce studded with clams, shrimp and crab. Fiends for variety can opt for sampler plates culled from the snaking antipasto bar, which offers cured meats, and an ocean of seafood.

restaurants.summary: Traveler is a laid-back bistro that celebrates Asian pop culture and flavors, changing with the seasons to bring a new destination into focus.
restaurants.description: Traveler is a laid-back bistro that celebrates Asian pop culture and flavors, changing with the seasons to bring a new destination into focus. Created by Gulp and 929, the journey moves on each season with food, drink, music and atmosphere inspired by the next stop. Think of it as a travel magazine you can step inside. Each visit takes you on a trip to a destination in Asia. Traveler includes New York's first tea liquor machine—grab a shot glass, insert the coin, and enjoy. Modeled after the saké vending machines in Japanese train stations, this machine echoes the train station-inspired interior design of Traveler and features a selection of tea-infused liquors, Taiwanese bubble tea shop-inspired liqueur, and the famous kinmen kaoliang.

restaurants.name: Travelers Poets & Friends
restaurants.summary: Travelers Poets & Friends captures the essence of the Italian coastline with its authentic offerings.
restaurants.description: Travelers Poets & Friends captures the essence of the Italian coastline with its authentic offerings. Proprietor Emanuele Nigro, known for Osteria57 and Alice, has created a multi-faceted venue with a bakery, espresso bar, and market. The eatery offers breakfast, lunch, and dinner menus curated by Italian chef Riccardo Orfino, emphasizing seasonal ingredients and pescatarian-friendly dishes. Highlights include tuna Bolognese lasagna, grilled fishes, and eclectic pizzas. The marketplace section provides fresh and dry pasta, exotic salts, spices, and specialty drinks. Nigro's dedication to sustainable and high-quality seafood is evident, and the venue's ambiance reflects his Italian culinary philosophy.

restaurants.description: Located in a historic enclave, Tudor City Steakhouse is a "next generation" steakhouse, offering dishes not typically associated with the genre. Besides USDA Prime Beef, dry aged on-site, they salute their location just across the street from the United Nations with a selection of international dishes such as sushi ceviche, pasta and tamale. The relaxed elegance of their dining rooms and the the flexible flow of their bi-level space make Tudor City Steakhouse an option for a wide range of occasions, from romantic dining a deux or happy hour gatherings to receptions for 300.

restaurants.summary: Tuome is a critically acclaimed East Village restaurant by chef/owner Thomas Chen, whose ingredient-driven contemporary American menu showcases his classic culinary training with Asian influences.
restaurants.description: Tuome is a critically acclaimed East Village restaurant by chef/owner Thomas Chen, whose ingredient-driven contemporary American menu showcases his classic culinary training with Asian influences. The menu features items like octopus with pork XO sauce; chicken liver mousse with New York maple; and crispy deviled eggs with chili; and larger dishes like chicken porridge with basil sauce, and fan favorite, Pig Out for two (Berkshire pork, spicy peanut noodle and condiments), along with sides like sticky rice with duck fat. Evoking the East Village's relaxed character, the intimate space showcases rustic reclaimed materials given a modern update.

restaurants.description: Twin Tails is a new Thai and Vietnamese restaurant from Quality Branded, the team behind Bad Roman, Zou Zou’s, and other Manhattan staples. The menu includes fresh crudos, bright, herbaceous salads and small bites, and entrée favorites like Tiger Prawn Pad Thai, Red Curry Sea Bass, and the best-selling Cho Lon Duck. On the beverage side, the cocktail menu features a new take on the Lychee Martini and many fun riffs that will soon become signatures, while the wine list has strong French influence with entire sections dedicated to Sancerre, demi-secs, and vintage Bordeaux. Twin Tails is located within The Shops at Columbus Circle, and is open for lunch and dinner daily.

restaurants.name: Veeray da Dhaba
restaurants.summary: Founded by Michelin-starred chef Hemant Mathur, Veeray Da Dhaba brings Punjabi food to the East Village, celebrating slow-cooked classics, vibrant spices and the warm hospitality of Punjabi culture.
restaurants.description: Founded by Michelin-starred chef Hemant Mathur, Veeray Da Dhaba brings Punjabi food to the East Village. The menu celebrates slow-cooked classics, vibrant spices and the warm hospitality of Punjabi culture. From sarson da saag to tandoor-grilled specialties, Veeray da Dhaba invites guests to experience Indian cuisine as it was meant to be enjoyed—bold, soulful and shared with friends.

restaurants.name: Veerays
restaurants.summary: Located in Manhattan's Midtown East, Veerays is NYC’s first Indian speakeasy restaurant, envisioned by Michelin-starred chef Hemant Mathur.
restaurants.description: Veerays is NYC’s first Indian speakeasy restaurant, envisioned by Michelin-starred chef Hemant Mathur. Located in Manhattan's Midtown East, Veerays redefines Indian cuisine with a menu of innovative curries and grills. The intimate space captures the allure of the 1920s Prohibition era, serving signature cocktails inspired by the era, alongside a meticulously curated selection of wine, beer, and spirits. Reservations are recommended, but walk-ins are warmly welcomed. Veerays the ideal destination for an unforgettable culinary experience.

restaurants.name: Verde on Smith
restaurants.summary: Verde on Smith is Cobble Hill, Brooklyn's neighborhood eatery, featuring regional Italian cuisine complemented by friendly service and warm ambiance.
restaurants.description: Since 2009, Verde on Smith has been Cobble Hill, Brooklyn's neighborhood eatery, featuring regional Italian cuisine complemented by friendly service and warm ambiance. The menu is characterized by fresh, simple, but flavorful ingredients—the essence of Italian cuisine—specializing in fresh and delicious Italian seafood, pasta, appetizers, and tasty desserts. Paired with local brews, signature cocktails, and a wide selection of wine, there is something for everyone to enjoy. Verde on Smith's brunch and lunch menu offers a wide selection of burgers, savory and sweet brunch dishes such as French toast, omelets, pancakes, sandwiches, burgers, crepes, avocado toasts, fresh salads and more. At dinner, the menu highlights pasta, salads steaks, appetizers, chicken dishes and fresh seafood and fish.

restaurants.name: Veselka
restaurants.summary: Find 24-hour comfort food and Ukrainian specialties at this East Village standby.
restaurants.description: You can hardly call yourself a New Yorker without having a favorite dish at the famous East Village Ukrainian eatery Veselka Restaurant. In business since 1954, it offers neighbors and visitors 24-hour comfort food in a diner-type atmosphere. The kids love the pierogis and potato pancakes; the adults love the borscht and sweet cheese blintzes. On the way out it’s hard to pass up the pastry counter with its pies, cupcakes, cookies and homemade muffins. The restaurant also has a seasonal outdoor café.

restaurants.name: Via 13
restaurants.summary: Via 13, set in the West Village, serves the essence of Italy today—bold flavors, warm hospitality, and surprising twists make every visit unforgettable.
restaurants.description: Via 13 is the next chapter in the story of the West Village restaurant formerly known as Sotto 13. They've evolved—renovated, reimagined, and reenergized. So much has changed, it felt only right for the owners to change the name too. Via 13 serves the essence of Italy today—bold flavors, warm hospitality, and surprising twists make every visit unforgettable. It’s not a postcard from the past; it’s the next chapter in Italian dining.

restaurants.name: Victor's Cafe
restaurants.summary: Victor’s, in the Theatre District, has been a redoubt for high-end Cuban food since 1963.
restaurants.description: Victor’s, in the Theatre District, has been a redoubt for high-end Cuban food since 1963. In an airy space, the tropical theme is carried out with bright hand-painted murals, cane-backed chairs and old-time paddle fans gently waving in the rafters. The menu is more ambitious than a rice-and-beans joint, with both a classica menu of favorites like ropa vieja, skirt steak sautéed in onions, tomatoes, onions and peppers, then shredded by hand; and a nueva menu with ambitious fare like snapper, marinated in Seville oranges, and salmon, with a sugarcane glaze.

restaurants.name: Vin Sur Vingt - E. 51st St.
restaurants.summary: Vin Sur Vingt, from Sébastien Auvet (a wine enthusiast of the modern era, emphasizing simplicity, authenticity, and value), offers an impressive wine selection alongside a tapas-style French fare menu.
restaurants.description: Vin Sur Vingt is a French bistro on 51st Street in Manhattan's Midtown East, offering an extensive wine list and authentic French cuisine. Founded by wine enthusiast Sébastien Auvet, this intimate French restaurant features carefully curated wines emphasizing simplicity, authenticity, and exceptional value. The menu showcases classic French bistro fare, perfectly paired with selections from their impressive wine collection. With its charming Parisian atmosphere and prime Midtown location, Vin Sur Vingt is a top destination for wine lovers and French food enthusiasts seeking an authentic dining experience in New York City.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

restaurants.name: Viv
restaurants.summary: Viv is a design-forward Thai restaurant and cocktail bar in Hell’s Kitchen with a lively nightlife scene in later hours.
restaurants.description: Reimagined after 17 years on Ninth Avenue, Viv is a design-forward Thai restaurant and cocktail bar in Hell’s Kitchen on Midtown Manhattan's West Side. Helmed by master chef Verasak Sangsiri, the striking 70-seat space showcases refined regional Thai street food by day and NYC's first authentic late-night Khao Tom Feast by night—centering around a customizable porridge ritual. Viv features an exclusive, avant-garde beverage program designed by Bangkok’s world-renowned Mahaniyom cocktail bar (voted No. 19 in The World’s 50 Best Bars). Viv is perfect for Theatre District dining, date nights and late-night culinary gatherings.

The dishes are characterized by their polished adaptation of traditional Viennese and European classics, elegantly paired with a world-class wine list.

restaurants.description: “Wan Waan” refers to days long ago that are remembered through memories and stories. Times past are recalled through various stimuli, familiar things such as listening to music, viewing old pictures, atmosphere, or even gaining familiar tastes. It helps people to reminisce about the days that have passed. The team at Wan Waan, a Thai restaurant in the Chelsea neighborhood of Manhattan, emphasizes feelings through the taste of food. By stimulating positive emotions, the delicious tastes will bring guests nostalgic memories of the past and with it good memories. When diners make delicious memories together, then they will think of “Wan Waan” together.

restaurants.description: The Warren Street Bar & Restaurant is a modern neighborhood brasserie offering an all-day menu of much-loved classics and fresh, seasonal dishes filled with flavors and ingredients from around the world. The space itself is a celebration of color and creativity, with an eclectic art collection and characterful interiors. Executive chef Diego Chaparro was born in Lima, Peru, but most recently comes from Miami, Florida. His passion for storytelling throughout each dish stems from the relationship and connection he feels getting to work with local farmers and purveyors.

restaurants.name: Wayan
restaurants.summary: Intoxicating Indonesian food from a talented chef in Nolita.
restaurants.description: This beautifully designed Indonesian restaurant is the brainchild of Cédric and Ochi Vongerichten, a couple deft at providing wonderful food and hospitality. A bar and some small tables are up front; a narrow passage winds past the chef’s counter to an amber-lit dining room. Cédric (son of Jean-Georges) is both a gifted and rigorously trained chef, evidenced by lightly fried baby squid, intoxicating corn fritters, nasi goreng (fried rice with a runny egg) and noodles with lobster and basil. Don’t miss the sundae with bruléed bananas and violet-hued ube ice cream.

restaurants.name: Yakiniku Toraji An
restaurants.summary: Toraji is a "yakiniku" style BBQ restaurant that serves thicker cuts of meat to better convey their delicious taste.
restaurants.description: Toraji is a "yakiniku" style BBQ restaurant, and their first shop was established in 1995 in a small backstreet in Ebisu in Tokyo's Shibuya-ku. The owners felt that serving thicker cuts of meat would convey their delicious taste better, so they offered what at the time were unusually thick cuts. A meal starts with "namuru" and "kimchi" Korean-style steamed and pickeled vegetables, continuing with tongue, ribs and/or outside skirt, and finishes with cold noodles or a "pibimpab" Korean-style mixed rice bowl. Toraji is committed to providing guests withan authentic yakiniku experience.

restaurants.name: Yoon Haeundae Galbi
restaurants.summary: Owner Bobby Yoon started Yoon Haeundae Galbi to carry on his grandfather's legacy and bring authentic Korean food from Haeundae, Busan, South Korea to New York City.
restaurants.description: Owner Bobby Yoon started Yoon Haeundae Galbi to carry on his grandfather's legacy and bring authentic Korean food from Haeundae, Busan, South Korea to New York City. The restaurant 해운대암소갈비집, which was established in 1964 and has spanned three generations, remains a local favorite in Busan. All the short ribs are prepared using the Haeundae Cut, a special technique that was invented by Bobby's grandfather to tenderize even the toughest of meats. This method is something unique to their restaurant, and is the core of what makes their meat different from other establishments. Although the restaurant in NYC is a contemporary recreation of the one in Busan, the traditional roots on which Yoon Haeundae Galbi are built remain intact. The team has made a wholehearted effort to preserve these aspects in the midst of a city that modernizes by the second.

restaurants.description: Roberto Paciullo, a native of Salerno (a port city south of Naples) opened the original Zero Otto Nove ("089") on Arthur Avenue in 2008, named after Salerno's telephone area code. Riding a wave of Naples-style pizza fetishism, the place focused on pies, but a full southern Italian bill of fare was also available, delivered in belly-busting portions. This branch in the Flatiron District combines the menu of Paciullo's other Bronx outpost, Roberto's Restaurant, with that of the original Zero Otto Nove.

restaurants.name: Zoì Mediterranean UES
restaurants.summary: Blue Mezze Bar - UES is a unique Mediterranean restaurant/bar on Manhattan's Upper East Side with an extensive mezze and cocktail menu, ideal for sharing and tasting.
restaurants.description: Blue Mezze Bar - UES is a unique Mediterranean restaurant-bar on Manhattan's Upper East Side. It has an extensive mezze and cocktail menu, ideal for sharing and tasting—perfect for friends, family or that upcoming date. The Blue serves a Mediterranean menu with a modern twist—fresh fish, tenderloin, vegetables, salads, a noteworthy lentil dish and homemade signature hummus—designed to elevate the fresh ingredients to the next level.

restaurants.name: Zuma
restaurants.summary: Zuma, the brainchild of award-winning co-founder and creator Rainer Becker, brings its internationally acclaimed style of modern Japanese cuisine to Midtown Manhattan.
restaurants.description: Zuma, the brainchild of award-winning co-founder and creator Rainer Becker, brings its internationally acclaimed style of modern Japanese cuisine to Midtown Manhattan. Zuma serves dishes designed to share that are inspired by the informal dining style of izakaya. Its three kitchens present authentic yet alluring options, with bold flavors and simple presentation, highlighting quality ingredients.
